items.t: Meet the Black woman helping people buy land for less than $1,000 in just 5 days
items.x: For Black families, land has always meant more than property. It has meant freedom, stability, power, security, and something tangible to pass down. But over the last century, Black land ownership has declined dramatically. The Federation of Southern Cooperatives reports that Black farmland ownership peaked at roughly 16 to 19 million acres in 1910 and has fallen to less than 3 million acres today. The organization also estimates that more than 60% of Black-owned land is heirs’ property, leaving many families vulnerable to losing land that was meant to remain in the family. The ownership gap is still visible today. According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the Black homeownership rate was 44.0% in the first quarter of 2026, compared with 75.0% for non-Hispanic White households. items.t: Ex-NFL Player Jon Vaughn: ‘Who Protects Us from Our Protectors?’
items.x: By Jon Vaughn, Contributor I ended my last piece with a question, and I want to be honest about why I asked it. I did not pose it as a rhetorical flourish. I asked it because survivors have asked it of me, on the phone, late at night, after discovering what had been done with their names, their stories or their trust by people who said they were on their side. I asked it because I have had to ask it myself, about a room I walked into carrying evidence and walked out of as the problem. Who do I go to? Too often the true answer was: right now, nobody. That is not an accident. It is a design. We built our protectors the way the institutions built theirs. Every institution I have ever fought had the same shape. Power sat with one office. items.t: Elon Musk-Linked Network Funded Cornel West’s 2024 Ballot Push: Report
items.x: A conservative political network with financial ties to billionaire Elon Musk helped fund efforts to get independent presidential candidate Cornel West on state ballots during the 2024 election, according to a new investigation. The findings, published Monday (October 26) by Sludge , shed new light on the financial backing behind West's candidacy, which Democrats feared could draw votes away from Kamala Harris and help Donald Trump win the presidency . West, a prominent Black scholar and progressive activist, ran on a platform focused on racial justice, economic equality and opposition to U.S. military intervention. During the election, Democrats raised concerns that West could serve as a spoiler candidate in competitive states. The Associated Press separately reported that groups with Republican ties in Virginia, North Carolina and Arizona were working to help West secure ballot access.

items.t: Young Black Georgians Drive Sharp Rise in Early Voting Ahead of Midterm Elections
items.x: With Election Day approaching, a notable shift is emerging in Georgia's early voting numbers: Black residents, particularly younger voters, are casting ballots at a substantially faster pace than they did during the last midterm election. An analysis by a Democratic data firm found that early in-person voting among Black Georgians increased 33% during the first nine days of voting compared with the corresponding period in 2022. Participation among voters younger than 30 rose 54%, while the increase among young Black voters reached 80%. The figures, first reported by The Atlanta Journal-Constitution, offer an early look at who is participating in an election that will determine Georgia's next governor and a U.S. Senate seat. items.t: Chris Brown Receives Suspended Sentence In London Nightclub Brawl
items.x: Thaddaeus McAdams Chris Brown won't be going to jail despite pleading guilty in a London court following a 2023 nightclub brawl. The 37-year-old R&B star was sentenced to eight months in prison, suspended for 12 months, meaning he won't serve any time as long as he stays out of trouble. Brown was convicted of affray, which in the British justice system involves the use or threat of unlawful violence. He pleaded guilty on July 24 after denying more serious charges of attempting to cause grievous bodily harm and assault causing actual bodily harm, which prosecutors later dropped. Affray carries a maximum sentence of three years in prison. The charges stem from a 2023 incident at Tape, a private members' club in London's Mayfair neighborhood. items.t: Drake s "Janice STFU" Copyright Lawsuit Thrown Out
items.x: XNY/Star Max / Drake A copyright infringement lawsuit against Drake over his recent hit “Janice STFU” was dismissed less than two weeks after filing. According to reports, rapper/songwriter Aviel Hirschfield filed a motion in federal court on Tuesday (October 27) to dismiss his lawsuit against Drake. He offered no explanation for filing the motion in the letter requesting the dismissal. The Portland, Oregon-based Hirschfield filed his lawsuit against Drake on October 16, alleging that the Canadian star copied the entire chorus he wrote specifically for “Janice STFU”, which has gone on to be a major hit from Drake’s Iceman album. Hirschfield claims that he wrote the chorus in January, inspired by Swedish singer Lykke Li. “This song was written specifically for Drake using music provided to [Hirschfield] that was created by Drake’s producers,” Hirschfield’s representative said at the time.

items.x: JC Olivera Eric Bauza brought Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, and a long list of cartoon favorites to a new generation of viewers. The Emmy-winning voice actor has died at 46. As spotted on Complex , Bauza’s family announced his death Sunday (Oct. 25) in a statement posted to his Instagram account. Variety reports that Bauza died at his home from hypertensive cardiovascular disease, citing records from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner. His family described his passing as sudden and said more information would follow. Born Dec. 7, 1979, in Scarborough, Toronto, Bauza was the son of Filipino immigrants . His interest in animation began when he watched classic cartoons as a child, with the original Looney Tunes performances shaping his ambitions. He graduated from Centennial College in 2000 and went on to build his career in Hollywood. His path to the microphone started on the drawing board.

items.t: Nathan Brown, convicted in 1976 murder of Bonnie Bolluch, released from prison and out on parole
items.x: CSRA (WJBF) – A man who was sentenced to life in prison in for a 1976 murder is now out on parole. Nathan Brown was released from prison on Tuesday, Oct. 27. He was convicted in the 1976 murder of Bonnie Bulloch in Taliaferro County . Bulloch, 11, was at a Crawfordville gas station with his stepfather, who was working a night shift, when he and his stepfather were kidnapped. A group of men, including Brown, shot Bulloch and his stepfather in the head. His stepfather survived and identified the killers. Brown, Jose High and Judson Ruffin were convicted of murder and sentenced to death in 1979. However, Brown and Ruffin got new trials and were resentenced to life in prison. Jose High was put to death in 2001. Ruffin remains in prison.

items.t: Former WJBF sports director Stan Byrdy dies at 73
items.x: WJBF is saddened to announce that longtime sports anchor Stan Byrdy has died. Byrdy was Sports Director at WJBF from 1985 to 1994 and remained on the station's Masters Tournament coverage team through 2002. He later served as Sports Director at WAGT-TV in Augusta from 2006 to 2009. After his television career ended, he wrote four books on local history including "Alister Mackenzie's Masterpiece: Augusta National Golf Club". A local historian, he was a popular guest on talk shows and podcasts nationwide. He also served as coordinating executive producer for the Emmy-nominated documentary, “Augusta’s Master Plan; From Sherman’s March to Arnie’s Army”, for Georgia Public Broadcasting. Stan is survived by his wife and two children. He was 73.

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

items.t: New SNAP rules for South Carolina start Nov. 1
items.x: SOUTH CAROLINA (WJBF) Beginning November 1st, South Carolina will update the definition of SNAP-eligible foods. Candy, energy drinks, soft drinks, and other sweetened beverages will no longer be allowed for purchase with SNAP benefits. Diet and zero sugar soft drinks are allowed. This is all part of the Healthy Food SC project, a two-year initiative designed to help households receiving SNAP benefits make healthier food choices. The goal of this project is to promote healthier food choices among participants by encouraging the purchase of more nutritious foods while reducing the purchase of items with limited nutritional value. All South Carolina SNAP approved retailers will participate in this project, and SNAP households in South Carolina will not have the option to opt out of these food restrictions. For more information on the new program, please visit the Healthy Food SC website .

items.t: 40 new jobs coming to Edgefield County with expansion of poultry plant
items.x: EDGEFIED COUNTY, S.C. (WJBF) Amick Farms , a poultry processor in Batesburg, announced that it's expanding with a new operation in Edgefield County. The company’s $54.78 million investment will create 40 new jobs. The company already has four existing complexes: two in Saluda County, one in Laurel, Mississippi, and one in Hurlock, Maryland. Amick Farms’ new hatchery, located in Trenton, will have the capacity to hatch over 1.5 million eggs, supporting the growth of the company’s South Carolina poultry processing operations. Operations are expected to be online in April of 2027. Individuals interested in joining the Amick Farms team should visit the company’s careers page . The Coordinating Council for Economic Development awarded a $1 million Set-Aside grant to Edgefield County to assist with the costs of site preparation and building construction.

items.t: 68 dead in high-speed train collision, Spain’s 2nd deadly rail crash this year
items.x: URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in Spain on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. The collision came just nine months after another deadly crash involving high-speed trains operated by the same two companies in southern Spain in January. “Today all of Spain is grieving,” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of national mourning. items.t: Utah authorities connect 1974 cold case to serial killer Ted Bundy
items.x: SUMMIT COUNTY, Utah ( KTVX ) — Investigators in Summit County, Utah closed the 1974 cold case homicide of Melissa Ann Smith Tuesday, linking her murder to prominent serial killer Ted Bundy. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. items.t: New South Carolina law protects abuse victims under 18
items.x: SPARTANBURG, S.C. (WSPA) Gov. Henry McMaster joined state legislators, law enforcement officers and prosecutors at the South Carolina Statehouse last Thursday for a ceremonial bill signing of Senate Bill 405. The legislation expands South Carolina's Homicide by Child Abuse statute to cover victims under age 18. McMaster officially signed Senate Bill 405 into law on March 9, 2026. The measure closed a legal gap in the previous statute, which capped the maximum age of a victim under the law at 11 years old. Under the previous statute, a gap existed in which children between 12 and 17 years old were excluded from being classified as victims of homicide by child abuse. If a child older than 11 suffered from and succumbed to abuse or neglect, prosecutors were required to try offenders for murder or other criminal offenses instead of the specialized child abuse homicide charge.

items.t: SNAP winners and losers: Which states are facing possible funding cuts?
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – Time is ticking for states to slash their error rates or risk losing a sizable amount of federal funding for SNAP. The pressure comes from a law passed last year that ties error rates to federal funds for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program, or SNAP, the program formerly known as Food Stamps. States need to meet a target error rate under 6% to avoid being impacted, but so far only a small minority have made the cut. As of the 2025 fiscal year , only nine states had error rates under 6% and 41 states were still in trouble. What are SNAP error rates? The error rate refers to the percentage of SNAP benefits paid either above or below what people should have received, primarily because of mistakes. items.t: Single Mothers Need Work Schedules They Can Count On
items.x: By Chastity Lord, President and CEO, Jeremiah Program A work schedule can determine whether a mother keeps her childcare, attends class, or makes it to a medical appointment. When that schedule changes with little warning, she has to rebuild all three arrangements while protecting the paycheck that pays for them. Employers should treat predictable scheduling as part of what makes a job sustainable. For a single mother, the hours attached to a job are part of its compensation. A wage offer means less if she cannot estimate how many hours she will receive. A promotion can be difficult to accept if its schedule makes reliable childcare impossible. In truth, we have long been at the heart of both. It used to be normal to grow your own food and contribute with a village mindset, so it came naturally for generations past to build a community with these practices centered on sustainability and nourishment. Today, however, we are more separated from the land and the growing process than ever. With food security and environmental justice so tightly wound together, that distance has harmed both our food landscape and our physical one. To advance food justice and heal our environment, we must return to the practices of our ancestors which still run through us. items.t: Building a village of care for South Side families
items.x: Family caregivers make it possible for older adults to remain at home, but love alone cannot carry the weight. Keeping older parents safe and out of a nursing home can feel intense–the 3 a.m. worries, the chores and errands, the distractions from a full-time job. The loss of "me time" can feel deeply isolating, but it’s a true blessing to be able to take care of your family. I know this journey well. My father was the primary caregiver for my grandmother for more than a decade as she battled dementia. I saw the loneliness of his journey, the physical and mental drain, and the immense sacrifices he made to be present for his mother while raising a family of his own. I’ve felt the same things caring for my husband after his multiple sclerosis diagnosis. Balancing life, work, and family priorities can be all-consuming. items.t: Surrounded By People But Still Lonely? Here s Why It Happens And Tips To Feel More Connected

items.t: Louisiana teen makes history after being cured of sickle cell anemia
items.x: Phillip Mullin, a 15-year-old from Louisiana, has triumphed over sickle cell anemi a after being hospitalized over 100 times due to complications from the disease. Thanks to a groundbreaking gene therapy, he is now considered functionally cured. His mother, Shataka Figgins, reflected on their challenging journey during an emotional celebration on October 23 at Manning Family Children's Hospital . I remember every sleepless night, and every moment I wondered how much more his body could take, but I will also see the young man who made it through, she told WVUE Fox 8 . Mullin is the first child in Louisiana to be considered cured of sickle cell disease, according to WVUE FOX 8. He is also the first person in the state to receive LYFGENIA, a groundbreaking one-time gene therapy tailored specifically for each patient using their own stem cells. Local reports indicate that since May, over 4,800 people have died in DR Congo and that is its deadliest outbreak of the disease, leading to a massive spread of the virus to other African nations. These restrictions in Uganda come after two people who had travelled through the country tested positive for Ebola, in Kenya and Nigeria. Shelby and her son and daughter soon began searching for a place to rent and ended up buying a house that is three times the value of Michael Jackson's home and others in the neighborhood, according to the Chicago Crusader. Actually, Shelby was not aware that her house was located next to the Jackson family home until her daughter Ebony went to see the house upon learning it was for sale. items.t: North Korea targeting cash-strapped Americans in expanding job scam: FBI
items.x: The FBI is warning Americans about an expanding North Korean scheme that uses fake job opportunities, stolen identities and unsuspecting U.S. residents to infiltrate American companies and help finance the country's nuclear weapons program. In an Oct. 13 public safety alert , the agency said thousands of state-controlled North Korean information technology workers are using increasingly sophisticated tactics to secure remote jobs at Western companies while concealing their identities and locations. Federal investigators warned that the workers are now recruiting Americans, particularly those experiencing financial hardship, to help carry out the fraud, sometimes without realizing they are assisting a foreign government. items.t: Southern California sex trafficker sentenced to 74 years to life in prison

The investigation began on July 9, 2023, when Long Beach police responded to reports of a “person in distress” near 67th Street and Long Beach Boulevard. At the location, officers found a teen girl who was a trafficking victim. During their investigation, detectives learned the suspect had driven the girl to Los Angeles to work as a commercial sex worker. “While the victim was being sex trafficked, she was physically and sexually assaulted,” police said. The British actor-comedian entered Southwark Crown Court alongside his wife, Laura Gallacher, to testify in his own defense, telling reporters that “today is the day for truth and justice.” Brand, 51, stood in the witness box and took the oath, then gave his full name: Russell Edward Brand. items.t: Frontier Airlines airfare jumps 71% in third quarter
items.x: High fuel prices are squeezing just about all of us, and they're having a major impact on the transportation industry. Frontier Airlines, the country's largest budget carrier, just revealed in its third quarter, their fares jumped 71% because of soaring jet fuel costs. The carrier's fare revenue averaged almost $68 per passenger in that quarter, compared with about $40 a year earlier. Then you tack on fees for baggage and seating and other services, and suddenly total revenue per passenger was up 30% to $138. These higher fares illustrate how sky-high energy costs related to the war in Iran are slamming the economy, impacting consumers from the gas pump to the airline terminal. In the heart of South L.A.'s Adams District, The Reset Room is creating a peaceful escape from the hustle and bustle of everyday life. Founded by certified yoga instructor Adriana Gasaway, this wellness experience combines breathwork, meditation, and sound healing to help guests relax, recharge, and learn techniques to regulate their nervous systems. Gasaway's journey into wellness began during the pandemic when she launched Ace Naturals, her skincare and body butter line. Today, she's expanding her mission from nourishing the body to nurturing the mind and spirit. LA Unscripted's Jasmine Simpkins stopped by Violet Noir, the event space where The Reset Room hosts classes every Tuesday and Thursday, to learn how a little intentional stillness can go a long way toward finding balance. items.x: Party Goats La brings unforgettable fun, charm and a little farmyard magic to celebrations or brush clearings throughout Los Angeles. The friendly, lovable goats make unique guests at birthday parties, hikes, private events, school gatherings, yoga classes and special celebrations of all kinds. After losing her home and floral studio in the Altadena fire, Ortega relocated her business to North Hollywood, where she's continuing to blossom. LA Unscripted's Jasmine Simpkins visited her showroom to hear about her journey, which includes being selected for FIFA's small business supplier program to provide floral arrangements for SoFi Stadium during the World Cup. No stranger to large-scale projects, Ortega has delivered anywhere from 1,200 to 1,500 floral arrangements in a single week! From corporate clients to weddings, parties, and private events, she says no job is too big or too small. Her philosophy? items.t: Your One-Stop Beauty Escape: Inside Milk + Honey Spa
items.x: A little milk, a little honey, and a whole lot of pampering! Inspired by Cleopatra, who was famously said to bathe in milk and honey to maintain her beautiful skin, Milk + Honey Spa is putting a modern twist on the royal treatment. Founded in Austin, Texas in 2006, the luxury day spa has expanded to 10 locations nationwide over the past two decades. LA Unscripted's Jasmine Simpkins stopped by the Brentwood location to chat with community manager Lexie Bennett about the brand's growth and its mission to create a one-stop destination for beauty and wellness. From massages and facials to waxing, nail services, and even injectables, Milk + Honey offers a full menu of treatments in a serene, Zen-inspired setting designed to help guests relax, recharge, and leave feeling like royalty. items.x: Step into the wonderfully weird world of The Mystic Museum in Burbank, a one-of-a-kind destination celebrating horror movies, the supernatural, the occult and all things delightfully macabre. Located in the eclectic Magnolia Park neighborhood, this immersive attraction combines unusual curiosities, vintage oddities, gothic treasures and ever-changing exhibits inspired by cult horror films and pop culture. Visitors can explore interactive installations, shop the unique collectibles and capture unforgettable photos in movie-inspired settings. Whether you’re a lifelong horror fan, a lover of the unusual or simply looking for an extraordinary Los Angeles experience, the Mystic Museum is your one-stop shop. Greenville Police Department officials said that Panettiere's death has been ruled accidental, based on findings in the investigation and the medical examiner's determination. On August 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive in an apartment at the Judson Mill Lofts on Easley Bridge Road. items.t: Prince Jackson hopes to finally make ‘Thriller’ hit No. 1
items.x: Michael Jackson's song "Thriller" was released over 40 years ago, and it remains a hit. While the "Thriller" album spent a record-breaking 37 weeks on the Billboard 200, the single itself only reached the No. 4 spot in 1984. Jackson's eldest son, Prince, and fans of the King of Pop want to change that with the "Thriller Challenge." "You've got the album that is stacked with incredible songs, right? So the goal is to try and get my father's song Thriller,' the single, to number one," he explained on the KTLA 5 Morning News. "The way that we encourage people to do that is to request the play from radio stations, buy the single, buy the vinyls, the albums, and stream it as much as you can, because we are trying to get my father another number one." items.t: American naturalization rates have declined ‘sharply,’ new research finds
items.x: Naturalization rates have declined “sharply” across America, with California particularly affected, according to new research . The study, conducted by experts from UCLA’s Center for Neighborhood Knowledge, determined that becoming a United States citizen has “become increasingly more difficult” by analyzing changes in national and state rates of naturalization. The findings: there were 76% fewer legal immigrants gaining citizenship nationwide under the administration of President Donald Trump as compared to the administration of President Joe Biden. At a broader scope, UCLA experts say that annual naturalization rates grew “dramatically” between the 1990s and 2024, by which time the monthly average was over 70,000. items.t: Southern California’s coastal flooding is a problem now. Expert warns it could get worse
items.x: From San Diego to Los Angeles, coastal communities are getting inundated as high tides have sent ocean water cascading over berms and boardwalks, flooding roads, homes and businesses . Newport Beach’s Balboa Peninsula and the International Boardwalk in Redondo Beach were among the areas that saw flooding on Tuesday, and more flooding is expected in the coming days. Experts say ocean water levels are shattering records this fall due to several factors converging all at once: long-term sea-level rise, normal tides caused by the pull of the sun and the moon, and the emerging effects of a “super” El Niño , a periodic warming of ocean temperatures in the tropical Pacific. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

The annual study estimates attendance at many of the world's most popular theme parks. Most theme park operators do not publicly disclose official attendance figures. Attendance at the world's leading theme parks was essentially flat in 2025. The top 25 parks drew a combined 245.4 million visits, compared with 245.9 million visits for the same parks in 2024, a decline of 0.2%, according to the report. items.t: Lawsuit accuses Los Angeles animal rescue of puppy laundering
items.x: The Los Angeles City Attorney's Office announced a lawsuit Tuesday against an animal rescue operation for allegedly purchasing dogs from puppy mills and reselling them to adopters as "rescued" animals. items.t: Could hackers shut off your water? SoCal agencies prepare
items.x: Cyberattacks don’t just put personal information at risk. They could also disrupt essential services, including the water systems we depend on every day. “So you could have a wastewater plant that’s completely down. You could have a water district that can no longer serve the 150,000 customers that they intended to serve, right? And then they could actually replicate that through different water districts or different agencies,” said Ephraim Gonzalez of TEC-Refresh. That’s why local water agencies are teaming up through a regional cybersecurity coalition called ERNIE. The goal is to share information, strengthen their defenses and practice how to respond if hackers get into their systems. One concern is the automation used to operate water systems. “So if they control the automation, then they can change chemical amounts. But there’s set points to stop that. items.t: Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight we’ll lose
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – With daylight saving time coming to an end this weekend , many of us are about to see our latest sunsets until February. In some parts of the country, the last sunset at 6 p.m. or later will happen before our clocks even fall back. Our clocks being set back an hour early Sunday morning will, of course, cause early sunsets. That's the trademark of standard time , shifting sunlight toward the morning and away from the evening. But the natural tilt and orbit of Earth as we glide toward winter are also contributing to days feeling shorter , at least in terms of the sunlight we get to experience. As part of that, many in the U.S. recently had their final sunset after 6 p.m. until well into 2027. items.t: New SNAP rules for South Carolina start Nov. 1
items.x: SOUTH CAROLINA (WJBF) Beginning November 1st, South Carolina will update the definition of SNAP-eligible foods. Candy, energy drinks, soft drinks, and other sweetened beverages will no longer be allowed for purchase with SNAP benefits. Diet and zero sugar soft drinks are allowed. This is all part of the Healthy Food SC project, a two-year initiative designed to help households receiving SNAP benefits make healthier food choices. The goal of this project is to promote healthier food choices among participants by encouraging the purchase of more nutritious foods while reducing the purchase of items with limited nutritional value. All South Carolina SNAP approved retailers will participate in this project, and SNAP households in South Carolina will not have the option to opt out of these food restrictions. For more information on the new program, please visit the Healthy Food SC website .

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

items.x: SOUTH CAROLINA (WCBD) The South Carolina Department of Social Services on Wednesday announced that its new program, Healthy Food SC, will take effect on Sunday. Healthy Food SC project is a two-year initiative beginning on Nov. 1, updating the definition of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)-eligible foods by removing candy, energy drinks, soft drinks, and other sweetened beverages. Diet and zero-sugar soft drinks will still be SNAP-eligible after the new definitions take effect. This change will affect all South Carolina SNAP-approved retailers. SNAP households will not have the option to opt out of the restrictions. More information about the program can be found on dss.sc.gov .

items.t: The Odd Savannah: Uncovering the city’s haunted history
items.x: SAVANNAH, Ga. (WSAV) — Savannah is known for its beautiful weeping willow trees and historic charm. But beneath the beauty lies something odd! The Odd Savannah is a show that focuses on everything odd in the spookiest city in the South. In its premiere episode, host Elliot Rosenblatt sits down with paranormal investigators Micah Watkins and Courtney Knight as they untangle nearly 209 years of history and haunts of the Savannah Theatre. From stories about its connection to renowned 19th-century actor Edwin Booth, brother of Abraham Lincoln’s assassin, John Wilkes Booth, to urban legends about the ethereal tenants that roam the theatre, this interview will unravel stories that go beyond the history books.

items.t: 68 dead in high-speed train collision, Spain’s 2nd deadly rail crash this year
items.x: URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in Spain on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. The collision came just nine months after another deadly crash involving high-speed trains operated by the same two companies in southern Spain in January. “Today all of Spain is grieving,” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of national mourning. items.t: Recalled butter sold in 10 states receives risk warning: FDA
items.x: NEW JERSEY ( WPIX ) A popular plant-based butter has been recalled due to yeast, mold and E. coli, and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration has now assigned it a risk level . The recall, which was initiated by Prosperity Organic Foods, Inc., headquartered in Boise, Idaho, involves 1,304 cases of Miyoko's Creamery European Style Salted Plant Milk Butter. items.t: Mexican sex offender, who entered U.S. illegally five times, sentenced to 3 years in prison
items.x: ROCKFORD, Ill. (WTVO) — A Mexican national, previously accused of sexually assaulting a minor, has been sentenced to 3 years in prison for illegally re-entering the U.S. multiple times after being caught in Harvard, Illinois. The U.S. Department of Justice said Francisco Hernandez-Ramos, 51, was arrested in Harvard, Illinois, on August 7. At that time, he had been deported from the United States five times and was in the country illegally. Hernandez-Ramos had previously been convicted of criminal sexual assault of a minor, attempted possession of child pornography, illegal entry, and illegal re-entry. He pleaded guilty in June 2026 in federal court in Rockford to one count of unlawful re-entry after removal. On Tuesday, he was sentenced to three years in federal prison. He is expected to face deportation proceedings once he serves his sentence.

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

"As a non-medical home care agency owner, I've seen how the generational differences in caregiving can shape the way we support older adults in their homes," Prussak said. items.x: BYRON, Ill. (WTVO/WQRF) — The U.S. Department of Energy has agreed to loan Constellation Energy up to $5 billion for major upgrades at the Byron Nuclear Plant. items.t: Sunshine and 70s return Wednesday, Clouds move back in late week
items.x: Clouds filled our skies Tuesday afternoon but that didn't stop temperatures from reaching the upper 60s in northern Illinois. When you look at radar you will notice a little green showing up indicating some precipitation moving through the region but given our dry atmosphere not much if any of that is actually reaching the ground. This means that we'll just continue to see mostly cloudy skies for the remainder of the evening. These clouds have been the result of a weak low-pressure system (upper-level disturbance, really) moving through the Midwest. It's pulled in a little more moisture which has led to the increase in cloud cover. But late tonight that low will move out which will help clear our skies into the overnight and bring temperatures down into the mid-40s once again. There may even be some patchy fog early Wednesday. items.t: Cause of death revealed for ‘Office Space’ actor Richard Riehle: Reports
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – The cause of death for longtime actor Richard Riehle has been revealed, according to reports. The 78-year-old died earlier this month in Los Angeles, friends told TMZ , which was the first to report the news. The outlet and People , citing his death certificate, reported Tuesday that the "Office Space" actor experienced a stroke and had oropharyngeal cancer. He had been in a rehabilitation center at the time of his death in mid-October, according to People. Oropharyngeal cancer , which can be asymptomatic, impacts the middle portion of your throat, including the base of your tongue and the tonsils. While there are multiple types of oropharyngeal cancers, Johns Hopkins Medicine says the majority are squamous cell carcinomas, which are further divided into HPV-related and HPV-unrelated. The former is caused by HPV, while the latter is commonly caused by tobacco or alcohol. Deta

items.t: Heavy fire breaks out at Rockford home causing $60,000 in damages
items.x: ROCKFORD, Ill. (WTVO) — A fire at a home in Rockford late Tuesday morning caused approximately $60,000 in damages, officials reported. According to the Rockford Fire Department, firefighters were called to the 3400 block of Elm Street around 11:32 a.m. and found heavy fire coming from the front of the home. Officials said the fire was brought under control through the effort of 19 firefighters in under 15 minutes. No injuries were reported, and the Illinois State Fire Marshal's Office and Nicor Gas personnel were called in to assist with the investigation. The cause of the fire is undetermined, officials said.

items.t: Electrical fire triggers evacuation at Harlem Middle School
items.x: LOVES PARK, Ill. (WTVO) — Harlem Middle School students were evacuated Tuesday afternoon due to an electrical fire in the girls' locker room, according to fire officials. First responders were called to the school, located at 735 Windsor Road, around 2:15 p.m. According to a letter sent to parents by Principal Jerry Harris, the fire occurred in an electrical panel. Emergency responders cleared the building for students and staff to return at approximately 2:35 p.m., Harris said. "We are pleased to report that all students and staff are safe," he wrote. items.x: JANESVILLE, Wis (WTVO) — A Janesville man was arrested after officers found a deceased person inside an apartment Sunday, according to the Janesville Police Department. Police said officers responded to the 800 block of Myrtle Way for a welfare check. While investigating the call, officers found a person dead inside the apartment. items.t: Do Rockford residents really pay the highest property taxes in America? Here’s what the numbers show
items.x: ROCKFORD, Ill. (WTVO) — Few claims are repeated more often in Rockford than the belief that local residents pay the highest property taxes in the country. The statement is easy to understand. Tax bills have climbed for many homeowners over the last decade, and national studies routinely place the Rockford metropolitan area near the top of the country when measuring property tax burdens. But whether Rockford has the nation's highest property taxes depends on how the question is asked. If the measurement is property taxes as a percentage of a home's value, Rockford frequently ranks among the highest-taxed metro areas in America. If the measurement is actual tax dollars paid each year, many homeowners in communities such as Naperville, Oak Brook, Hinsdale, Barrington, Lake Forest and parts of Crystal Lake often pay substantially higher taxes than the average Rockford homeowner. (WTVO) — The Rockford City Council voted 11-1 to advance a proposed framework for data centers, sending the proposal to the Zoning Board of Appeals for public hearings in November. items.x: ROCKFORD, Ill. (WTVO) — Four Texas men are charged after Rockford Police said 12 pounds of cocaine were recovered during a narcotics investigation Monday. Around 10 a.m. Monday, the Rockford Police Department and the Drug Enforcement Administration conducted a narcotics investigation in the 7600 block of Colosseum Drive. Authorities said 12 pounds of cocaine were recovered during the investigation. Four men — 43-year-old Cesar Alvarez-Pineda, 24-year-old Israel Alvarez-Molina, 22-year-old Raul Santos-Sanchez and 24-year-old Jesus Ramon-Ramirez, all of Texas — were taken into custody. The Winnebago County State's Attorney's Office authorized charges of possession of a controlled substance with intent to deliver against all four men. They were booked into the Winnebago County Jail and are awaiting a pretrial hearing.

items.t: Union officer recognized for helping elderly man
items.x: UNION, Ohio ( WDTN ) – The Union Police Department is recognizing Officer David Clarkston for helping a man with dementia back on Tuesday, Oct. 20. Clarkston received a report that an elderly man suffering from dementia had gotten lost while driving in the area. Although information suggested the vehicle was in another county, Clarkston remained on alert. Within minutes, he saw the car traveling through the city and conducted a traffic stop. Clarkston was able to ensure the man was safe and contact his son, who helped his father get home safely. “This is a great example of what policing is all about,” wrote the UPD. “It’s not always about making arrests or issuing citations. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

He was 92. Nominated by then-President Bill Clinton in 1998, Hellerstein oversaw many high-profile disputes during his nearly three decades on the bench in New York City. He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. Maduro and his wife were in the judge's courtroom less than two weeks ago to plead not guilty to a new set of criminal charges. Before the Maduro operation, Hellerstein had long clashed with President Donald Trump in court. "We are deeply saddened to announce that our beloved mother, Dolores Huerta, has passed away today at the age of 96," her family said in a statement posted on social media. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. items.t: Bees and wasps becoming more aggressive in the fall months
items.x: DAYTON, OHIO ( WDTN ) Bees and other stinging insects are preparing for the winter months, and you may have noticed yourself swatting more and more at them. The fall months signify the end of the growing season, meaning lower food totals. The yellow jacket is the most aggressive of the stinging insects, due to the way it feeds. Stephanie Murray, University of Dayton PHD Candidate in insect ecology, said, “Workers will hunt other insects, and they don't eat those insects, but they actually feed them to their larvae or their babies. And in return, the larvae will actually secrete a nutritious, sugary substance that the adults will eat. “As the summer ends and the fall begins, the larval population is dwindling. items.x: (NEXSTAR) – The cause of death for longtime actor Richard Riehle has been revealed, according to reports. The 78-year-old died earlier this month in Los Angeles, friends told TMZ , which was the first to report the news. The outlet and People , citing his death certificate, reported Tuesday that the "Office Space" actor experienced a stroke and had oropharyngeal cancer. He had been in a rehabilitation center at the time of his death in mid-October, according to People. Oropharyngeal cancer , which can be asymptomatic, impacts the middle portion of your throat, including the base of your tongue and the tonsils. While there are multiple types of oropharyngeal cancers, Johns Hopkins Medicine says the majority are squamous cell carcinomas, which are further divided into HPV-related and HPV-unrelated. items.t: 21-year-old motorcyclist dead following Elmhurst crash
items.x: ELMHURST, Ill. — A 21-year-old man on a motorcycle died following a crash in Elmhurst Tuesday afternoon. Just before 4:30 p.m., authorities responded to reports of a serious crash at Grand Avenue and Lamont Road. At the scene, police found a box truck and a Honda motorcycle in the roadway. The driver of the motorcycle, a 21-year-old man from Glendale Heights, was pronounced dead at the scene. The road was closed until approximately 10:15 p.m. Police believe the motorcyclist was traveling westbound on Grand Avenue and the box truck was traveling the opposite way when they collided in the intersection. The box truck driver remained at the scene.

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

items.t: ‘Artificial Intimacy: Who We Become When We Talk to Machines’
items.x: If social media came for our attention, artificial intelligence is now coming for our capacity for attachment. items.t: No clear winner yet in Israel’s national elections: What happens now?
items.x: JERUSALEM (AP) — No clear winner has emerged in Israel’s national elections as vote-counting continues, and weeks of negotiations may lie ahead as Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his main rival, Gadi Eisenkot, will scramble to build a governing coalition. The election was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu , the country’s longest-serving prime minister, who gave a defiant speech to his supporters just after 3 a.m. on Wednesday in Jerusalem despite the unclear results. With around 70% of the votes counted on Wednesday afternoon, his party, Likud, appears to have gotten the most votes, capturing around 20% of the popular vote. This was a dip from the previous election in 2022, when Likud won 23.4% of the popular vote. items.t: Cause of death revealed for ‘Office Space’ actor Richard Riehle: Reports
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – The cause of death for longtime actor Richard Riehle has been revealed, according to reports. The 78-year-old died earlier this month in Los Angeles, friends told TMZ , which was the first to report the news. The outlet and People , citing his death certificate, reported Tuesday that the "Office Space" actor experienced a stroke and had oropharyngeal cancer. He had been in a rehabilitation center at the time of his death in mid-October, according to People. Oropharyngeal cancer , which can be asymptomatic, impacts the middle portion of your throat, including the base of your tongue and the tonsils. While there are multiple types of oropharyngeal cancers, Johns Hopkins Medicine says the majority are squamous cell carcinomas, which are further divided into HPV-related and HPV-unrelated. He was then taken to the Wildlife Center of Virginia for rehabilitation, but couldn't be safely released into the wild since he had already become used to people. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

items.t: Smoking withdrawal symptoms and 7 ways to beat them
items.x: Smoking withdrawal is the set of symptoms your body and brain go through after you stop using nicotine, including strong cravings, irritability, anxiety, low mood, restlessness, trouble sleeping and difficulty concentrating. Symptoms are usually strongest in the first few days and ease over the next few weeks, according to federal health resources, though occasional cravings can pop up later. The good news is that they are temporary, and there are proven ways to make them easier to handle. Why does smoking withdrawal hit so hard? Nicotine reaches the brain within seconds and triggers dopamine, the chemical tied to reward. Over time, your brain adjusts to that steady supply. When it stops, your body protests. Many smokers mistake withdrawal symptoms for everyday stress, so a cigarette feels like relief when it is really just ending the withdrawal it caused. According to a review in JAMA b

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

items.t: New York State Unified Court System issues official guidance to prevent AI hallucinations
items.x: ALBANY, N.Y. (NEXSTAR) — The New York State Unified Court System warned lawyers on Monday to fact-check artificial intelligence tools before submitting legal papers to judges. The Advisory Committee on Artificial Intelligence and the Courts published a guide for attorneys to prevent fake cases and citations from entering the legal record. “The Risks of Using Artificial Intelligence in Preparing Court Papers: What Every Attorney Should Know” builds on previous rules adopted by the state court system . It tells lawyers using generative AI—computer programs like large language models that write text—to understand how the technology works and independently verify every fact, quote, and claim the software offers. The artwork spans the side of a 29-story building in the Morrisania Air Rights Development along East 158th Street between Morris and Park avenues. Standing nearly 300 feet tall, the mural is visible across the surrounding community and it is being called the tallest in the nation. Neighbors gathered Tuesday for a ribbon-cutting ceremony. The piece was created through a collaboration between residents, tenant leaders and the nonprofit organization ArtBridge. Neighbors participated in workshops throughout the year, helping shape the imagery and themes featured in the artwork. items.x: NEW YORK (PIX11) Dollar General shoppers in New York will see changes aimed at preventing overcharging after a state investigation found customers were often charged with incorrect prices. The news comes as the discount retailer faces a separate federal lawsuit over similar allegations. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced a settlement with Dollar General on Oct. 15. The company must donate $1.875 million worth of food and personal items to Foodlink, a Rochester-based nonprofit, and make changes to prevent customers from being overcharged. The state investigation found pricing problems at Dollar General stores across New York. The attorney general’s office reviewed more than 900 store inspection reports from 2021 to 2023. items.t: Queens man charged with murder after woman found in shallow grave
items.x: QUEENS, NY (PIX11) A 26-year-old man has been charged with murder after a 35-year-old woman was found in a shallow grave in Queens, police said. Rogelio Lozano-Garita was arrested Monday and charged with murder, criminal possession of a weapon, concealment of a human corpse and tampering with physical evidence, according to NYPD. Seraphina Pereira was found near Beach 58th Street and Almeda Avenue around 9:42 p.m. Saturday, police said. Officers responded to a 911 call and found Pereira unconscious and unresponsive. EMS workers pronounced her dead at the scene. The city’s chief medical examiner later determined Pereira’s death was a homicide, police said. Sources previously told PIX11 News that Pereira’s ex-boyfriend was accused of killing her. Sources also said she had been a victim of domestic violence. Pereira was a mother of four.

items.t: Monica Money Matters: Chase New Jersey, Expungement & Second Chance Clinic
items.x: Monica Makes It Happen is in Kearny, New Jersey, where our partners at JPMorgan Chase are helping change lives, one second chance at a time! items.t: What to Change When Your First Song Demo Doesn't Sound Right

Pick the first passage that bothers you and replay it. Before rewriting anything, work out whether the problem is the words, the way they're sung, or what's playing underneath them. When the words feel rushed Try singing the line over the existing tune. Where do you have to squeeze words in or cut a word short? Mark that spot. Suppose the line is “Today I'm going to take the long way home.” Try “I'll take the long way home.” You've kept the decision to take a longer route and removed the lead-in. items.t: John Legend Earns Music Matters Lifetime Honor

That included information on how it finds AI music and how much Suno material appears on its platform. Apple argued that testimony would expose private business information well beyond what Suno needed, Digital Music News reported . The singer-songwriter filed his copyright lawsuit against Trump 47 Committee Inc. on Monday, October 26, in Virginia federal court, according to Courthouse News Service . His complaint pointed to the song playing before President Donald Trump took the stage at an October 12 midterm campaign event in Youngstown, Ohio. The committee faced the claim, while Trump was not named as an individual defendant, Rolling Stone reported . Young also said the dispute carried a cost beyond the use of a recording: he claimed the association hurt his reputation by suggesting he backed Trump, according to TheWrap . items.t: Boosie Badazz Set To Perform With Full Orchestra In Little Rock

The Saturday night show will pair his Southern Hip-Hop catalog with The Signature Orchestra, giving fans a chance to hear his music backed by a live ensemble. The production draws on a recording career that spans more than two decades. "The Black Tie Experience was created to give audiences a different way to experience Boosie live," a Stage View Presents spokesperson said in an announcement published by SWARK Today . Robinson Center's performance hall seats 2,222. The venue dates to 1939 and underwent a $70 million renovation, according to its website. items.t: Nolan Wells March Brings Oxford Students Out For Answers
items.x: Nolan Wells name was back on signs at the University of Mississippi on October 25 as students and Oxford residents marched for answers about his death. University of Mississippi freshmen Christopher Burnett and Avah Trevino organized the event, The Daily Mississippian reported. They walked from Fulton Chapel past the Walk of Champions, the Circle and James Meredith's statue before returning. "We just want, simply, for the family's questions to be answered in further investigation," Burnett said. The demand had also reached Rider University, where its NAACP college chapter held an October 22 walk, according to The Rider News . President E'miija Eccles brought campus Black organizations into the event and contacted Public Safety three weeks ahead. Participants made at least three laps around Centennial Lake. Founding chapter president Naa'san S.J. Carr, a 2024 graduate, returned to speak.

items.t: Megan Thee Stallion Explains How Silence Over Her Contract Led To Regret & Legal War
items.x: Megan Thee Stallion said she once feared questioning her record deal. She spoke at Overcoming Impossible Live at 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge in New York City. Entrepreneur and Robert Irvine organized the event for business owners. The program paired small-group work with afternoon talks from Megan, Gary Vaynerchuk and Irvine. "I was a little bit nervous about asking questions," she told Entrepreneur . What followed were years of fights over her music. As AllHipHop previously reported, Megan signed with Carl Crawford's 1501 Certified Entertainment in 2018 and sued the label in 2020. In October 2023, the two sides settled and parted ways. They kept the terms private. During that dispute, Megan accused 1501 of blocking releases and keeping her under contract after she had fulfilled its terms. She also sought outside oversight of the label's finances to ensure it could pay a potential judgment.

Players present their mixes, vote and earn Season Tickets, which unlock Hit-Boy beat packs, clothes and DJ decks. Some packs can be earned through play, while players can also buy music and merchandise in the game, the report said. Those tools have a limit: Roblox won't let players export raw audio or separate vocal stems. The official Beat Battle page lists the Hit-Boy season as live. items.t: Hip-Hop Partnerships Are Changing the Commercial Value of Sports Events
items.x: Sports events used to build their commercial power around ticket sales, broadcast rights, and sponsor logos placed in predictable spots. That model still matters, but it no longer explains where the biggest cultural lift comes from. Hip-hop now shapes how events are packaged, promoted, and discussed long before the opening whistle or tip-off. When artists, teams, leagues, and media platforms align, they change what a sports property can sell and how far it can travel. The result is a stronger business engine: more attention, sharper identity, broader merchandise reach, and more digital touchpoints that keep fans connected between games. That shift is visible across major leagues, global tournaments, and event marketing strategies. items.t: Jay-Z Confirms Himself For Super Bowl Halftime Show At SoFi Stadium
items.x: Jay-Z will get his own turn on the Super Bowl halftime stage after years of helping other stars put their shows together. The NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation announced Monday that he will headline Super Bowl LXI on February 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. It will be his first Super Bowl halftime performance. His company has worked on the show since 2019, but the rapper had yet to take that stage himself. "Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world's biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true," Jay-Z said . items.x: ST. LOUIS – If you were to make a list of St. Louis landmarks, the one-of-a-kind Compton Hill Water Tower would likely be in the top five. The iconic Romanesque tower, located on one of the highest elevations in the city, used to provide water to people who lived in St. Louis. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

items.t: 4 in 10 say personal finances worsening: Survey
items.x: ( The Hill ) Four in 10 Americans say their personal finances are deteriorating, according to a new poll released shortly before November's midterm elections. In the NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll , 40 percent of people said their “personal family finances” have declined in the last 12 months, while 16 percent said the opposite. Forty-one percent said their personal family finances have “stayed about the same” within the prior year. Less than 1 percent of poll respondents were not sure about the state of their personal family finances within the last year, while three percent didn’t give an answer. The NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll was conducted two weeks out from Election Day, with the rise in cost of living being a major concern in this election cycle. The 78-year-old died earlier this month in Los Angeles, friends told TMZ , which was the first to report the news. The outlet and People , citing his death certificate, reported Tuesday that the "Office Space" actor experienced a stroke and had oropharyngeal cancer. He had been in a rehabilitation center at the time of his death in mid-October, according to People. Oropharyngeal cancer , which can be asymptomatic, impacts the middle portion of your throat, including the base of your tongue and the tonsils. While there are multiple types of oropharyngeal cancers, Johns Hopkins Medicine says the majority are squamous cell carcinomas, which are further divided into HPV-related and HPV-unrelated. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

The Beekse Bergen Safari Park said in a statement that the woman, whose name has been withheld in accordance with Dutch privacy law, had passed away after she suffered serious wounds to her head and neck on Saturday while working in an enclosure with two male Persian leopards. “Her passing deeply affects us all, and we sympathize intensely with her family, friends, and loved ones,” the zoo, in the southern town of Hilvarenbeek, said in a statement, which was made together with her family. The woman began working at the zoo when she was 17 and spent nearly all of her 40-year career there. items.t: Cause of death revealed for ‘Office Space’ actor Richard Riehle: Reports
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – The cause of death for longtime actor Richard Riehle has been revealed, according to reports. The 78-year-old died earlier this month in Los Angeles, friends told TMZ , which was the first to report the news. The outlet and People , citing his death certificate, reported Tuesday that the "Office Space" actor experienced a stroke and had oropharyngeal cancer. He had been in a rehabilitation center at the time of his death in mid-October, according to People. Oropharyngeal cancer , which can be asymptomatic, impacts the middle portion of your throat, including the base of your tongue and the tonsils. While there are multiple types of oropharyngeal cancers, Johns Hopkins Medicine says the majority are squamous cell carcinomas, which are further divided into HPV-related and HPV-unrelated. items.t: Days will get way shorter in November: How much daylight we’ll lose
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – With daylight saving time coming to an end this weekend , many of us are about to see our latest sunsets until February. In some parts of the country, the last sunset at 6 p.m. or later will happen before our clocks even fall back. Our clocks being set back an hour early Sunday morning will, of course, cause early sunsets. That's the trademark of standard time , shifting sunlight toward the morning and away from the evening. But the natural tilt and orbit of Earth as we glide toward winter are also contributing to days feeling shorter , at least in terms of the sunlight we get to experience. As early voting continues across Arkansas, the Garland County Election Commission is working from a repaired building months after winter weather damaged its roof and put hundreds of thousands of dollars in voting equipment at risk. items.t: Lake Maumelle nears historically low level, officials explain why they aren’t concerned
items.x: ROLAND, Ark.- Lake Maumelle is in rough shape, to say the least. If you visit it today, you'll see boats sitting in mud at the marinas, debris washed ashore, and that the shoreline has drastically decreased. Lake Maumelle is one of the primary sources of water for Central Arkansas Water customers, along with Lake Winona. The Public Affairs Officer with Central Arkansas Water, Douglas Shackleford, says the water level at Lake Maumelle is reaching historically low levels. "Lake Maumelle is definitely low. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

items.t: Five pets died, two people displaced by Norfolk house fire
items.x: NORFOLK, Va. (WAVY) — Three dogs and two cats died, and two adults have been displaced, as a result of a house fire Wednesday on Buckingham Street, just off of Chesapeake Boulevard. Norfolk Fire-Rescue responded to a reported structure fire at 8:30 a.m. and found heavy smoke and flames coming from a house. Firefighters initiated a fire attack, and a search confirmed that all occupants were outside the home. However, several pets were still inside. Photos courtesy of Norfolk Fire-Rescue The fire was brought under control at 9:12 a.m. Three dogs and two cats died as a result of the fire, while two adults were displaced and are requesting assistance from the American Red Cross, Norfolk Fire-Rescue said. The cause of the fire is still under investigation.

items.x: VIRGINIA BEACH, Va. (WAVY) Two people required assistance after a recreational boat ran aground on a stump Tuesday afternoon near the North Landing Bridge, according to the Virginia Beach Fire Department. Units were dispatched to a report of a boat in distress near the North Landing Bridge at approximately 3:15 p.m. Upon arrival, crews located a 40-foot recreational boat that had run aground on a stump and was listing to the starboard side. Authorities said two people aboard reported they were not in distress but needed assistance getting off the boat. They safely took both individuals to shore. items.t: Texas says 9 islands in Rio Grande belong to state, not Mexico

For years, river islands have provided what officials says are safe havens for cartels that smuggle drugs and migrants into the U.S. from Mexico, giving them a place to hide and wait out border patrols in those areas. A couple years ago, however, the Texas General Land Office declared some islands a part of the state and cleared them of vegetation. Some islands have had military troops land on them recently, and some are also used as border security staging zones. items.x: EL PASO, Texas (Border Report) — Florida authorities announced charges Tuesday against 10 people accused of participating in a Sinaloa cartel-linked cocaine network that used El Paso as a transportation hub for shipments to the Tampa Bay area. Investigators allege the organization moved cocaine from Mexico through El Paso before transporting it across the country in commercial trucks. El Paso police and Homeland Security Investigations assisted Florida detectives, authorities said. Prosecutors described the operation as a Juárez-based branch of the Sinaloa cartel that supplied Florida with monthly cocaine shipments from at least December 2025 through July 2026. Investigators say traffickers used inoperable truck tractors as cover to transport cocaine from El Paso to Florida as part of an alleged Sinaloa cartel-linked network. items.t: Utah authorities connect 1974 cold case to serial killer Ted Bundy
items.x: SUMMIT COUNTY, Utah ( KTVX ) — Investigators in Summit County, Utah closed the 1974 cold case homicide of Melissa Ann Smith Tuesday, linking her murder to prominent serial killer Ted Bundy. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. "The work began with the investigators who handled the case in 1974, and it continued through the dedication and perseverance of those who carried it forward," Summit County Sheriff Kacey Bates said. items.x: ( The Hill ) Four in 10 Americans say their personal finances are deteriorating, according to a new poll released shortly before November's midterm elections. In the NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll , 40 percent of people said their “personal family finances” have declined in the last 12 months, while 16 percent said the opposite. Forty-one percent said their personal family finances have “stayed about the same” within the prior year. Less than 1 percent of poll respondents were not sure about the state of their personal family finances within the last year, while three percent didn’t give an answer. The NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll was conducted two weeks out from Election Day, with the rise in cost of living being a major concern in this election cycle. items.t: Cause of death revealed for ‘Office Space’ actor Richard Riehle: Reports
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – The cause of death for longtime actor Richard Riehle has been revealed, according to reports. The 78-year-old died earlier this month in Los Angeles, friends told TMZ , which was the first to report the news. The outlet and People , citing his death certificate, reported Tuesday that the "Office Space" actor experienced a stroke and had oropharyngeal cancer. He had been in a rehabilitation center at the time of his death in mid-October, according to People. Oropharyngeal cancer , which can be asymptomatic, impacts the middle portion of your throat, including the base of your tongue and the tonsils. While there are multiple types of oropharyngeal cancers, Johns Hopkins Medicine says the majority are squamous cell carcinomas, which are further divided into HPV-related and HPV-unrelated. items.t: Yes, you still need an air purifier in the winter
items.x: BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission. Details. Air purifiers are really beneficial all year The first chilly night of fall usually means it’s time to close the windows and turn on the heat. And heaters are equipped with air filters, which means you can pack up the air purifier until spring, right? Maybe not. Dust, pet dander, cooking fumes and fireplace smoke can concentrate indoors during the cold months , and with windows closed against the cold, some of those pollutants can linger longer than they would when fresh air is circulating freely. According to Filtrete , air quality can worsen in winter thanks to tightly sealed windows, running your heating system and using fireplaces. The 37-year-old R&B star was sentenced to eight months in prison, suspended for 12 months, meaning he won't serve any time as long as he stays out of trouble. Brown was convicted of affray, which in the British justice system involves the use or threat of unlawful violence. He pleaded guilty on July 24 after denying more serious charges of attempting to cause grievous bodily harm and assault causing actual bodily harm, which prosecutors later dropped. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

items.t: NC boy still recovering after I-85 crash that killed mom, dad, and sister in Granville County

The Granville County crash was reported around 4 a.m. Saturday, Sept. 20, on northbound Interstate 85 near mile marker 197 at the Smith Road overpass, according to the North Carolina State Highway Patrol. A Charlotte family of four was traveling north in a Toyota Highlander when the driver of the SUV smashed into the back of the fire truck that was stopped on I-85 for an earlier crash, Sgt. A.A. Chehaitli of the highway patrol told CBS 17. Troopers said they believe the father who was driving fell asleep. items.x: CLAYTON, N.C. ( WNCN ) — A woman is dead after being hit by a pickup truck in Johnston County Tuesday morning, the North Carolina State Highway Patrol said. According to the NCSHP, 33-year-old Ashley Fuller of Johnston County was walking east on Rock Pillar Road near Clayton with her brother just before 9 a.m. when she was hit by a westbound pickup truck. Fuller was pronounced dead at the scene, according to the NCSHP. Troopers said Fuller and her brother were walking in the direction of the pickup truck at the time of the crash. Fuller's brother managed to avoid the vehicle, according to the NCSHP. According to the NCSHP, Fuller had just left her home and the crash happened near where she lived.
