items.t: After weeks, bedbug infestation cleared from Raleigh’s Oberlin library, Wake County officials say
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) — A bedbug infestation that lasted for more than a month in a Raleigh library has been cleared out, according to Wake County officials. Nearly two weeks ago — on Oct. 16 — a bedbug cleanup had already been underway for more than four weeks at the Oberlin Regional Library in the 1900 block of Clark Avenue in the Village District shopping area, according to a manager at the facility, which is part of the Wake County Public Library system. After the cleanup, according to Wake County officials, a follow-up inspection was held three days later, on Oct. 19, that confirmed the library was cleared of bedbugs. Wake County officials also said there were reports of bedbugs at other library locations, but those were unconfirmed. items.t: Candy Corn: A sweet debate among Americans this Halloween season
items.x: As Halloween approaches, one treat continues to spark debate among candy lovers: candy corn. According to recent research conducted by the National Confectioners Association, the iconic triangular candy remains a polarizing symbol of the spooky season. The survey reveals that a significant majority of Americans—60%—prefer to eat the entire piece of candy corn at once. However, consumption methods vary widely: 28% of candy corn fans start with the narrow white end, while 12% start with the wide yellow end. This split shows how personal the enjoyment of candy corn can be. No matter how you eat it, candy corn undeniably holds a special place in Halloween festivities. It continues to rank among the season's top treats, alongside beloved favorites like chocolate bars, gummy candies, and hard candies. Curated by renowned expert Robbie Smith, this exhibition tells a unique story rooted in Eastern North Carolina's culture and traditions. "We are excited to explore the interconnectedness of people, wildlife, and landscapes through the lens of sporting art, folk art, and fine art," said CAM representatives. The exhibition aims to bridge the rich local traditions with broader narratives in American art history, highlighting how these elements have shaped the region. items.t: Wake County-led workplace board wins over $ 5 million to help laid-off workers
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) — The Capital Area Workforce Development Board has been awarded a $5.8 million federal grant to help dislocated job seekers in Wake County and surrounding areas return to work. The 36-month initiative targets 628 laid-off workers across 15 North Carolina counties. Funded through the U.S. Department of Labor's Rapid Reskill Dislocated Worker grant program, the initiative focuses on employers rebuilding the regional industrial base. The effort concentrates on high-growth sectors, including advanced manufacturing and construction companies that adopt new technology. Wake County Commissioner Shinica Thomas emphasized the importance of supporting dislocated workers through local training and industry partnerships. “Losing a job can create real uncertainty for individuals and families and we want to help people get back on their feet as quickly as possible,” Thomas said.

items.x: CHAPEL HILL, N.C. ( WNCN ) — Hubert Davis, the former North Carolina men's basketball player and most recently the program's head coach, has a new job just in time for the new season. Davis has been hired by TNT Sports to be a studio and game analyst for the 2026-27 season, according to CBS Sports. He will make his debut in the studio on Nov. 5 during the network's Big East and Big 12 tripleheader, the outlet said. It marks a return to the media side of the business for Davis, who spent seven years as a college basketball analyst with ESPN following the end of his NBA playing career in 2004. The Carolina alum was let go in late March after the Tar Heels lost in overtime in the first round of the NCAA Tournament to VCU. items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) — Our very dry pattern isn't letting up, now sitting at 10 straight days without rain at Raleigh-Durham International Airport. The double-digit number comes after a trend of every weekend this month seeing measurable rain through October 17 — the last time rain fell in the area. Only a few days remain until Halloween on Saturday, but we're expecting more zeros through the end of the month. That would bring our rain-free stretch to 14 days — a full two weeks. The last time we had a dry streak that long was back from May 26 to June 17 of this year, when we tallied 23 days with no rain. But even that isn't close to the all-time consecutive dry day record, which stands at 38 straight days from late September through early November in 2000. Volunteers and students recently spent days restoring some of the wooden windows that are nearly 75 years old. The building once served as home to one of North Carolina’s first African American Catholic congregations. Originally completed in the early 1950s, NCCU later purchased the structure and moved it to campus. items.t: Fayetteville moves forward with elevator for downtown parking garage after years of delays
items.x: FAYETTEVILLE, N.C. ( WNCN ) — After years of complaints about accessibility at a downtown Fayetteville parking garage, city leaders are moving forward with plans to install an elevator. The five-story public parking garage next to Segra Stadium opened in 2018 alongside the Fayetteville Woodpeckers stadium. But the developer never completed several parts of the project, including the elevator. The unfinished development was originally supposed to include a hotel and high-rise apartments above the garage, with retail space on the ground floor. Today, some storefronts remain unfinished, with no flooring and weeds growing inside. The lack of an elevator has frustrated people who use the garage, including Woodpeckers fans who park there for games. She and other shoppers we spoke with told us they’re surprised the retail giant is accused of bad pricing practices. "As far as I know, the savings are what they say, the discounts are what they're supposed to be, and the prices usually." items.x: WENDELL, N.C. ( WNCN ) — One of Wake County’s beloved Christmas light displays is preparing for its final season. The owner of the Lake Myra Christmas Light Show said this year will be the last after nearly three decades of holiday magic in Wendell. “It’s hard for me to say no because I’ve been doing it for so many years,” said Don Williams. Williams was emotional as he told CBS 17 News this was his last year setting up. "I do it for the kids, families and the people from all over the world that come out to see this,” Williams said. Williams said he started in 1997 with some lights right outside his home. Now it has expanded to a large site in downtown Wendell. This light show was one of the first and largest computerized Christmas light shows in North Carolina. items.t: NC’s State Health Plan taps retiree funds amid cash crisis, reaches deal with Atrium Health
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) — North Carolina's State Health Plan could run out of money by the end of the year, prompting its Board of Trustees to vote Tuesday to dip into retiree health funds to keep the plan afloat for its 750,000 members. The decision comes as the plan struggles to keep up with rising healthcare costs, with more members needing expensive medical care. "We have more folks that are sicker, utilizing more things and fewer people that are healthier utilizing less things," said State Health Plan Executive Administrator Tom Friedman The plan is counting on its new multitier provider network to help control costs. On Tuesday, it reached a deal bringing Atrium Health into that network, ending a legal battle between the two. ( WNCN ) — For the first time since being fired from the head coaching job at North Carolina State University, the winningest coach in the school's football program history spoke publicly. Dave Doeren was relieved of his duties over the weekend following a 31-28 loss to Stanford. Earlier this week, Athletic Director Boo Corrigan thanked Doeren for his tenure with the program, saying he represented the university with pride. items.t: Pedestrian dead after being hit by car on Wake Forest Road in Raleigh, police say
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) — A pedestrian is dead after being hit by a vehicle in Raleigh late Monday night, police said. According to the Raleigh Police Department, officers responded just before 10:30 p.m. to a report of a crash involving a pedestrian on Wake Forest Road near Dresser Court. A preliminary investigation shows the pedestrian was struck by a southbound Toyota Corolla while crossing Wake Forest Road outside of a crosswalk, according to Raleigh police. Police said the pedestrian was taken to a local hospital, where they died from their injuries. The pedestrian has not been identified as of Tuesday morning. Police said the driver of the Toyota Corolla remained at the scene and cooperated with the investigation. As of Tuesday morning, no charges have been filed. The investigation into the crash is ongoing.

items.x: Farmers are a key voting group for Republicans, but their votes could be on the line, with the Iran war and President Trump’s tariff and trade wars driving up production costs along with diesel and fertilizer prices. The Trump administration has been rolling out financial assistance packages and projects for farmers in hopes of shoring up the electorate in next week’s midterm elections. Yet they may be right to be anxious about the voting bloc’s turnout. “Yes, I think they’re nervous. Frederiksen said farmers “don’t want to vote for a lot of the Democrats’ nonsense.” “They want to vote for Republicans, but this is their business, these are their families, and it doesn’t appear that anyone’s listening,” she said. items.t: Drug-resistant germs cause over 50,000 US deaths each year: CDC report
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) —Nineteen drug-resistant germs cause 9.7 million infections and 50,800 deaths in the United States each year, according to an updated threat assessment released by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The agency's 2026 AR Threats Report shows that health care-associated infections accounted for more than 42,000 deaths and nearly $12 billion in health care costs in 2023. The assessment categorizes 19 pathogens into four urgent threats, 13 serious threats and two concerning threats, while placing six additional pathogens on a Watch List for ongoing monitoring. items.t: Halloween stays dry, rain finally returns for November
items.x: The streak of dry weather will continue for the rest of the month, but it's looking more likely that rain will show up a few times the first week of November. Tuesday was our 10th day in a row with dry weather and there are several more dry days ahead, but Wednesday will bring something we haven't seen in a while: CLOUDS. Wednesday will have some clouds and fog, but still no rain. Sunshine will return later this week as temperatures will warm to near 80° by Friday. Halloween weekend will stay dry with just a very small chance of rain Sunday night. Mild temperatures will hold through the weekend too, including for trick-or-treat Saturday night. Next week continues to look like high pressure will finally move out and a pattern change will allow more moisture to return to central North Carolina. According to the Johnston County Sheriff's Office, 12-year-old AJ Paradise was riding his UTV on a private property along the 1300 block of Shaws Pond Road in Four Oaks when the side-by-side utility vehicle rolled over. Hundreds gathered Monday night with candles in hand to honor Paradise's life and show his family how loved he is. The Cumberland County Board of Commissioners voted 5-1 on Oct. 19 to direct staff to identify up to five alternative sites for the project. Commissioner Glenn Adams voted against the motion. items.t: NC State interim head football coach Todd Goebell speaks after Doeren firing
items.x: RALEIGH, N.C. ( WNCN ) — A 14-year era of NC State football is over after the university announced that head coach Dave Doeren was relieved of his duties over the weekend following a 31-28 loss to Stanford. Athletic Director Boo Corrigan thanked Doeren for his tenure with the program, saying he represented the university with pride. Doeren is the winningest head coach in Wolfpack history, leaving State’s sidelines with a 98-74 record and 10 bowl appearances, going 4-6 in postseason play. The team finished in the top 25 three times during his time in Raleigh, but a 10-win season eluded him throughout his tenure. NOW PLAYING Taking over the Wolfpack, at least for a short time, is Todd Goebbel. According to NC State, Goebbel has served as the coach for the team's running backs and is a special teams coordinator. He has been with the pack since 2019.

items.t: Judge rules James Comey’s daughter unlawfully fired as federal prosecutor
items.x: A federal judge ruled Monday that the Department of Justice (DOJ) unlawfully fired and must provide back pay to Maurene Comey, former FBI Director James Comey’s daughter who was terminated as a prosecutor last year. U.S. District Judge Jesse Furman rejected the Trump administration’s arguments that it had constitutional authority to fire her . “Defendants’ argument is contrary to an unbroken line of Supreme Court decisions dating back almost two centuries, and the Supreme Court itself has not formally overruled any of those decisions. That is sufficient, in itself, to reject the argument,” Furman wrote in his 55-page opinion . Maurene Comey has since taken another job and won’t be returning to the DOJ. items.t: Man killed in head-on crash on NC 98 in Wake County: NCSHP
items.x: WAKE FOREST, N.C. ( WNCN ) — A man is dead following a head-on crash in Wake County over the weekend, the North Carolina State Highway Patrol said. According to the NCSHP, the crash happened on Saturday around 12:30 a.m. on N.C. 98 near Ray Pond Road in Wake Forest. An investigation determined a 2007 Honda Accord was traveling east on N.C. 98 when it went over the left side of the road and struck a westbound 2019 Lexus RX350 SUV. Both vehicles came to a rest on the road, according to the NCSHP. Troopers said the driver of the Honda Accord died in the crash. He was identified as Moises David Bardales. According to the NCSHP, the driver of the SUV was not injured. Troopers said no charges are expected.

items.t: Small plane crashes in Edgecombe County, knocks down power lines: Sheriff
items.x: MACCLESFIELD, N.C. ( WNCN ) — A small plane crashed in Edgecombe County Monday morning, the sheriff's office said. Just after 10 a.m., the Edgecombe County Sheriff's Office announced a small plane crashed in the area of Stallings Road in Macclesfield. According to the sheriff's office, the plane landed too low and knocked down power lines. The pilot was able to safely exit the plane, according to the sheriff's office. Officials said the power lines remain down as of late Monday morning. The public is asked to avoid the area of Stallings Road while first responders are at the scene. The crash is under investigation by the North Carolina State Highway Patrol.

According to Travis County Fire Rescue, emergency crews responded to the crash and found six patients that needed help. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

If supporters gather enough signatures, Hutto voters would be asked in May 2027 whether to expand alcohol sales regulations across the city's current boundaries. How alcohol sales are regulated in Texas Depending on where you live in Texas, alcohol sales can be regulated differently. Counties, cities and even justice of the peace precincts generally fall into one of three categories: Dry: Alcohol sales are prohibited Wet: Alcohol sales are allowed under state and local law. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

items.t: Man charged with sending white substance to 4 lawmakers
items.x: ( The Hill ) – An Illinois man is facing federal charges related to mailing letters containing a white substance to four members of Congress this month in an act inspired by reports of suspicious packages being sent to dozens of lawmakers and election officials across the country. Matthew Unglesbee, 37, is charged with one count of false information and hoaxes and one count of mailing threatening communications, according to a criminal complaint unsealed Monday. He made an initial appearance in federal court via video on Monday afternoon. An accompanying affidavit states that FBI personnel responded to three congressional members’ offices in the Northern District of Illinois last Wednesday after receiving an anonymous tip. Letters containing a “white granular substance" — later determined to be salt — were found along with handwritten notes that read “HA HA,” according to the affidavit.

items.t: How Knox County keeps traffic moving amid population boom
items.x: KNOXVILLE, Tenn. (WATE) — There's a saying: "Numbers don't lie". If that's true, then Knox County is experiencing a population boom. According to World Population Review, Knox County has topped the half-a-million mark at 515,309, making it the third largest of Tennessee's 95 counties. According to the website Storage Cafe, approximately 5,000 to 8,800 people relocate to Knox County each year; that's roughly 2,035 families. With so many people relocating to the area, that means more cars and trucks on local roadways. If the average family has at least two cars, that means in a single year Knox County can see anywhere from 10,000 to 17,600 additional vehicles on county roads. "It is challenging for us," said Knox County Chief Engineer Jim Snowden. The court handed down the divided opinion on Friday, which means noncitizens do not have a constitutional right to challenge their detention, no matter how long they have been held. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

The election was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu , the country’s longest-serving prime minister, who gave a defiant speech to his supporters just after 3 a.m. on Wednesday in Jerusalem despite the unclear results. With around 70% of the votes counted on Wednesday afternoon, his party, Likud, appears to have gotten the most votes, capturing around 20% of the popular vote. This was a dip from the previous election in 2022, when Likud won 23.4% of the popular vote. items.t: Dolores Huerta, labor leader and activist, dies at 96
items.x: ( KTLA ) – Activist Dolores Huerta, who helped co-found the National Farm Workers Association with César Chavez, has died. She was 96. Huerta's family said in a statement through her foundation that she died Wednesday at home. "We are deeply saddened to announce that our beloved mother, Dolores Huerta, has passed away today at the age of 96," her family said in a statement posted on social media. "As you can imagine, this is an incredibly difficult time for us, and we ask for privacy as we grieve this incredible loss to our family," the statement continued. "We know that many of you around the world share in our mourning, and we will be following up on plans to recognize and celebrate her incredible life and legacy." Arrest documents show Rebecca Walpole and a male suspect entered the Madison, Tennessee, Home Depot on May 26 and rented a boom lift, which is commonly known as a cherry picker or basket crane. The equipment was towed using a silver Dodge Ram. According to court documents, the property was never returned. items.t: 68 dead in high-speed train collision, Spain’s 2nd deadly rail crash this year
items.x: URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in Spain on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. Rescue workers searched the wreckage through the day for survivors and bodies. The collision came just nine months after another deadly crash involving high-speed trains operated by the same two companies in southern Spain in January. “Today all of Spain is grieving,” Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said from the crash site, where he announced that his government would declare three days of national mourning. items.t: Utah authorities connect 1974 cold case to serial killer Ted Bundy
items.x: SUMMIT COUNTY, Utah ( KTVX ) — Investigators in Summit County, Utah closed the 1974 cold case homicide of Melissa Ann Smith Tuesday, linking her murder to prominent serial killer Ted Bundy. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. "The work began with the investigators who handled the case in 1974, and it continued through the dedication and perseverance of those who carried it forward," Summit County Sheriff Kacey Bates said. items.t: 4 in 10 say personal finances worsening: Survey
items.x: ( The Hill ) Four in 10 Americans say their personal finances are deteriorating, according to a new poll released shortly before November's midterm elections. In the NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll , 40 percent of people said their “personal family finances” have declined in the last 12 months, while 16 percent said the opposite. Forty-one percent said their personal family finances have “stayed about the same” within the prior year. Less than 1 percent of poll respondents were not sure about the state of their personal family finances within the last year, while three percent didn’t give an answer. The NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll was conducted two weeks out from Election Day, with the rise in cost of living being a major concern in this election cycle. items.t: Yes, you still need an air purifier in the winter
items.x: BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission. Details. Air purifiers are really beneficial all year The first chilly night of fall usually means it’s time to close the windows and turn on the heat. And heaters are equipped with air filters, which means you can pack up the air purifier until spring, right? Maybe not. Dust, pet dander, cooking fumes and fireplace smoke can concentrate indoors during the cold months , and with windows closed against the cold, some of those pollutants can linger longer than they would when fresh air is circulating freely. According to Filtrete , air quality can worsen in winter thanks to tightly sealed windows, running your heating system and using fireplaces. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

items.t: Texas says 9 islands in Rio Grande belong to state, not Mexico
items.x: HARLINGEN, Texas ( Border Report ) The State of Texas on Tuesday declared that nine river islands in the middle of the Rio Grande belong to the state, not to Mexico. For years, river islands have provided what officials says are safe havens for cartels that smuggle drugs and migrants into the U.S. from Mexico, giving them a place to hide and wait out border patrols in those areas. A couple years ago, however, the Texas General Land Office declared some islands a part of the state and cleared them of vegetation. Some islands have had military troops land on them recently, and some are also used as border security staging zones. items.t: Florida cocaine case exposes alleged Sinaloa cartel route through El Paso
items.x: EL PASO, Texas (Border Report) — Florida authorities announced charges Tuesday against 10 people accused of participating in a Sinaloa cartel-linked cocaine network that used El Paso as a transportation hub for shipments to the Tampa Bay area. Investigators allege the organization moved cocaine from Mexico through El Paso before transporting it across the country in commercial trucks. El Paso police and Homeland Security Investigations assisted Florida detectives, authorities said. Prosecutors described the operation as a Juárez-based branch of the Sinaloa cartel that supplied Florida with monthly cocaine shipments from at least December 2025 through July 2026. Investigators say traffickers used inoperable truck tractors as cover to transport cocaine from El Paso to Florida as part of an alleged Sinaloa cartel-linked network. items.t: Utah authorities connect 1974 cold case to serial killer Ted Bundy
items.x: SUMMIT COUNTY, Utah ( KTVX ) — Investigators in Summit County, Utah closed the 1974 cold case homicide of Melissa Ann Smith Tuesday, linking her murder to prominent serial killer Ted Bundy. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. "The work began with the investigators who handled the case in 1974, and it continued through the dedication and perseverance of those who carried it forward," Summit County Sheriff Kacey Bates said. items.t: Toyota recalls more than 228,000 vehicles over risk of injury
items.x: ( NewsNation ) — Toyota is recalling more than 228,000 vehicles due to an issue with the second-row seat backs that could increase the risk of injury, according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration. A notice by NHTSA says if a crash happens, the second-row seat backs may fail to remain secured. According to the notice, around 228,367 vehicles from the Toyota Sienna Hybrid 2022-26 are impacted. Dealers plan to update the supplemental restraint system electronics control unit software. For vehicles equipped with the “Mobility as a Service” package, dealers plan to replace the two second-row seat backs free of charge, according to NHTSA. Owners should expect to receive notification letters in the mail around Dec. 7, according to the notice. Close Thanks for signing up! Watch for us in your inbox. items.t: 4 in 10 say personal finances worsening: Survey
items.x: ( The Hill ) Four in 10 Americans say their personal finances are deteriorating, according to a new poll released shortly before November's midterm elections. In the NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll , 40 percent of people said their “personal family finances” have declined in the last 12 months, while 16 percent said the opposite. Forty-one percent said their personal family finances have “stayed about the same” within the prior year. Less than 1 percent of poll respondents were not sure about the state of their personal family finances within the last year, while three percent didn’t give an answer. The NPR/PBS News/Marist Poll was conducted two weeks out from Election Day, with the rise in cost of living being a major concern in this election cycle. items.t: Cause of death revealed for ‘Office Space’ actor Richard Riehle: Reports
items.x: (NEXSTAR) – The cause of death for longtime actor Richard Riehle has been revealed, according to reports. The 78-year-old died earlier this month in Los Angeles, friends told TMZ , which was the first to report the news. The outlet and People , citing his death certificate, reported Tuesday that the "Office Space" actor experienced a stroke and had oropharyngeal cancer. He had been in a rehabilitation center at the time of his death in mid-October, according to People. Oropharyngeal cancer , which can be asymptomatic, impacts the middle portion of your throat, including the base of your tongue and the tonsils. While there are multiple types of oropharyngeal cancers, Johns Hopkins Medicine says the majority are squamous cell carcinomas, which are further divided into HPV-related and HPV-unrelated. items.t: What to do if poll workers say you aren’t registered to vote
items.x: ( NewsNation ) – Turnout has been surging in early voting, with vote counts reportedly exceeding the numbers collected during early voting in the last midterm elections. But what happens if you head to the polls and you're told you aren't registered to vote? Whether you vote early or on Election Day, here's what to do if you're told you aren't eligible to vote. Check before you go Check your registration status online before you go to vote and make sure you have the correct address for your polling place. Update your registration If you have recently moved, your registration may still reflect your old address. Ask a poll worker if you can update your registration on site and vote, or if you'll need to go to your old polling place to cast a ballot. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

items.t: Feeling brave? A look inside ‘haunted’ places in Northeast Ohio
items.x: CLEVELAND (WJW) There's something unique about fall the leaves turn to hues of red and orange, the days grow shorter and an ominous chill fills the air. It's also a time when more people become intrigued by the unexplained. For those living in Northeast Ohio, you don't have to travel far to find something a little extra eerie this Halloween season. Whether it be personal stories, old legends, or visits by nationally-recognized paranormal investigators, Ohio is no stranger to reports of ghostly sightings and spooky spots. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

By late Halloween, our attention will turn to an approaching cold front and a developing area of low pressure that could bring showers and thunderstorms to the region. The front is expected to move through late Saturday into Sunday morning, bringing the potential for a few strong storms before the system clears the area. For now, enjoy the sunshine and warmer temperatures, but keep an eye on the forecast as we get closer to Halloween weekend. We’ll continue to monitor the timing of the front and any changes in the potential for strong storms.

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

items.t: Utah authorities connect 1974 cold case to serial killer Ted Bundy
items.x: SUMMIT COUNTY, Utah ( KTVX ) — Investigators in Summit County, Utah closed the 1974 cold case homicide of Melissa Ann Smith Tuesday, linking her murder to prominent serial killer Ted Bundy. Using DNA and other evidence, the Summit County Sheriff's Office and Summit County Attorney's Office formally closed the cold-case murder, saying that the evidence conclusively proves that Ted Bundy murdered 17-year-old Melissa Ann Smith. Bundy has long been considered a suspect in several cold cases in Utah, and Smith's murder was one of them. Hunters found her remains in Summit County on Oct. 27, 1974, 52 years ago today. "The work began with the investigators who handled the case in 1974, and it continued through the dedication and perseverance of those who carried it forward," Summit County Sheriff Kacey Bates said. "After 50 years, we have reached a point that so many have worked toward." Ted Bun

According to The Guardian , Claude exploited a loophole in an older version of the Georgia agency’s website, which issued digital access tokens that allowed users to reach the data. items.t: Man charged with sending white substance to 4 lawmakers
items.x: ( The Hill ) – An Illinois man is facing federal charges related to mailing letters containing a white substance to four members of Congress this month in an act inspired by reports of suspicious packages being sent to dozens of lawmakers and election officials across the country. Matthew Unglesbee, 37, is charged with one count of false information and hoaxes and one count of mailing threatening communications, according to a criminal complaint unsealed Monday. He made an initial appearance in federal court via video on Monday afternoon. An accompanying affidavit states that FBI personnel responded to three congressional members’ offices in the Northern District of Illinois last Wednesday after receiving an anonymous tip. Letters containing a “white granular substance" — later determined to be salt — were found along with handwritten notes that read “HA HA,” according to the affidavit.

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

Arrest documents show Rebecca Walpole and a male suspect entered the Madison, Tennessee, Home Depot on May 26 and rented a boom lift, which is commonly known as a cherry picker or basket crane. The equipment was towed using a silver Dodge Ram. According to court documents, the property was never returned. The male suspect was arrested in Michigan on Sept. 23, according to arrest documents. Investigators said he admitted to selling rented construction equipment to buyers on Facebook Marketplace. Walpole faces a felony theft of property charge, and she was recently booked in Davidson County. Her bond was set at $10,000.

items.t: Sugary foods to lose SNAP-eligibility on Nov. 1: SCDSS
items.x: SOUTH CAROLINA (WCBD) The South Carolina Department of Social Services on Wednesday announced that its new program, Healthy Food SC, will take effect on Sunday. Healthy Food SC project is a two-year initiative beginning on Nov. 1, updating the definition of Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)-eligible foods by removing candy, energy drinks, soft drinks, and other sweetened beverages. Diet and zero-sugar soft drinks will still be SNAP-eligible after the new definitions take effect. This change will affect all South Carolina SNAP-approved retailers. SNAP households will not have the option to opt out of the restrictions. More information about the program can be found on dss.sc.gov .

items.t: Rays ace Drew Rasmussen to start World Series Game 5 against Milwaukee
items.x: ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. (AP) — Drew Rasmussen will start for Tampa Bay on three days' rest in Game 5 of the World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers on Wednesday night, trying to stave off elimination for the Rays. A 31-year-old right-hander, Rasmussen threw 89 pitches over 3 2/3 innings in Game 2 on Saturday, getting no decision as Milwaukee rallied for a 5-4 victory and a 2-0 Series lead. Rasmussen has had three major elbow operations in his career, including Tommy John surgeries in 2016 and 2017 and an internal brace procedure in 2023. The two-time All-Star was 16-5 with a 2.67 ERA in the regular season. Jacob Misiorowski was to start on regular four days' rest for the Brewers, who have a 3-1 lead in the best-of-seven series after wasting a 12th-inning lead in a 4-3 loss Tuesday . items.t: ¿Tu vivienda sufrió daños por Helene o Milton? Hillsborough ofrecerá asistencia en tres comunidades con el programa “Rebuilding for Tomorrow”
items.x: TAMPA, FLA. (WFLA-TAMPAHOY) — El Condado Hillsborough abrirá en noviembre tres centros temporales de atención para ayudar a propietarios que reúnen los requisitos de ingresos y cuyas viviendas resultaron dañadas por los huracanes Helene o Milton en 2024. Los centros funcionarán un día cada uno en Mango, Brandon y Egypt Lake. Allí, los residentes podrán recibir ayuda para solicitar fondos del programa Rebuilding for Tomorrow, destinado a reparar o reconstruir viviendas afectadas por las tormentas. El condado también mantiene abierto un centro de servicios en 1029 E. Hillsborough Ave., Tampa, FL 33604. La sede atiende de lunes a viernes, de 8 a.m. a 5 p.m. Quienes necesiten ayuda con la solicitud pueden llamar al (813) 540-7767 durante el mismo horario. items.t: Muere a los 92 años Alvin Hellerstein, juez federal de casos de Trump y Maduro
items.x: NUEVA YORK (AP) — Alvin K. Hellerstein, juez federal de Manhattan que presidió casos relacionados con el presidente Donald Trump , el expresidente venezolano Nicolás Maduro y los atentados del 11-S durante casi tres décadas en el cargo, ha fallecido. Tenía 92 años. Hellerstein falleció el miércoles por la mañana rodeado de su familia, dijo la jueza principal Laura Taylor Swain en un comunicado. Su funeral está programado para el jueves en la Riverside Memorial Chapel de Manhattan. La jueza presidenta Laura Taylor Swain recordó a Hellerstein como un "jurista distinguido" y elogió su "servicio enérgico y dedicado" al tribunal, que se mantuvo hasta su muerte. "Se le agradece mucho y se le echará mucho de menos", dijo Swain. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

items.t: Judge overseeing Maduro trial dies
items.x: ( The Hill ) Alvin Hellerstein, a longtime federal judge who was set to oversee the criminal trial of deposed Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro, has passed away, according to a court official. He was 92. Nominated by then-President Bill Clinton in 1998, Hellerstein oversaw many high-profile disputes during his nearly three decades on the bench in New York City. He was back in the national limelight presiding over the proceedings for Maduro , who was captured and brought to the U.S. earlier this year over accusations of narco-terrorism. Maduro and his wife were in the judge's courtroom less than two weeks ago to plead not guilty to a new set of criminal charges. Before the Maduro operation, Hellerstein had long clashed with President Donald Trump in court. Huerta's family said in a statement through her foundation that she died Wednesday at home. "We are deeply saddened to announce that our beloved mother, Dolores Huerta, has passed away today at the age of 96," her family said in a statement posted on social media. "As you can imagine, this is an incredibly difficult time for us, and we ask for privacy as we grieve this incredible loss to our family," the statement continued. "We know that many of you around the world share in our mourning, and we will be following up on plans to recognize and celebrate her incredible life and legacy." items.x: TAMPA, FLA. (WFLA-TAMPAHOY) – Los vientos fuertes continuarán un día más. Será un día más bochornoso, con temperaturas máximas que rondarán los 84F y que se sentirán más altas esta tarde. items.x: URDA, Spain (AP) — A high-speed train slammed into another that had stopped on the tracks in Spain on Wednesday, killing at least 68 people and injuring dozens in the second deadly rail collision this year. The regional government of Castilla La Mancha confirmed the death toll and said another 58 people were receiving medical treatment at hospitals. items.t: Spring Hill woman arrested after fleeing trooper on US-19: FHP
items.x: SPRING HILL, Fla. (WFLA) — A Spring Hill woman is facing felony charges after leading a Florida Highway Patrol trooper on a chase on U.S. Highway 19, FHP said. The incident began just after 11:30 p.m. on Monday, Oct. 26, when the trooper was on Little Road and spotted a Hyundai Sonata traveling at high speeds. He activated his lights, but the driver, 33-year-old Camille Watson, continued and turned onto US-19. Watson pulled into a private driveway, and the trooper got out of his vehicle and instructed her to do the same. She stayed in the car, turned the lights off, and reentered US-19, continuing to flee southbound. At that point, the trooper performed a successful PIT maneuver, which ended the chase. Watson was arrested and has been charged with fleeing and eluding, driving under the influence, and received a citation for speeding.

He had been in a rehabilitation center at the time of his death in mid-October, according to People. Oropharyngeal cancer , which can be asymptomatic, impacts the middle portion of your throat, including the base of your tongue and the tonsils. While there are multiple types of oropharyngeal cancers, Johns Hopkins Medicine says the majority are squamous cell carcinomas, which are further divided into HPV-related and HPV-unrelated. Prior to the sighting, a paddleboarder in the area had warned Slavich about a great white shark nearby. Tallahassee Police Chief Lawrence Revell shared that a physical altercation between individuals who knew each other led to the gunfire. “At this stage of the investigation, none of the victims appear to have been the intended targets,” Revell noted. According to CNN , the injured include six juveniles, with the youngest being 11 years old. A victim’s grandmother was also hurt while fleeing. The incident occurred hours after FAMU's homecoming game at Bragg Memorial Stadium, though authorities have not confirmed a connection to the event. The investigation remains active, and police indicate that additional arrests are possible.

items.t: DC-Only vs. AC Portable Power Stations: Which Connections Do You Actually Need?
items.x: Choose a DC-only power station when your essential equipment can run directly from its USB and DC outputs. Choose a station with AC outlets when you need to operate an appliance through a conventional household plug. That decision becomes clearer when you list the actual connections your equipment requires. Battery capacity matters, but it cannot compensate for an output that cannot power an essential device. An AC Power Station Usually Gives You Both Types of Output The terminology can cause confusion. A station described as an AC model generally contains an inverter and household-style outlets, often alongside USB and DC connections. A DC-only model omits those household AC outlets. It supplies compatible devices through connections such as USB-C, USB-A, and a vehicle-style DC socket. Both store energy in a battery. Their practical difference is how that energy can reach your equipment

items.t: DOJ’s California ballot fight rejected by another judge
items.x: ( The Hill ) The Trump administration's bid to separate 20,000 mail ballots in California that it says are likely noncitizens met another defeat on Wednesday as a trial judge refused to intervene. items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

items.t: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady in face of persistent inflation
items.x: Federal Reserve officials held interest rates steady Wednesday despite stubborn inflation. The central bank's Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10-2 to keep the benchmark federal funds rate range at 3.75 percent to 4 percent. "The committee believes that the accumulation of more information will help it determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the 2 percent goal," Fed Chair Kevin Warsh told reporters, reiterating the FOMC's statement. Fed board of governors member Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland's president Beth Hammack dissented in favor of a quarter-point increase. Hammack also backed a rate hike in late July, joining two of her colleagues in the minority when the central bank kept rates steady . Wednesday's decision came six weeks after officials raised rates by a quarter point , the first hike in more than three years.

items.t: DOJ charges Comey for third time
items.x: Former FBI Director James Comey has been charged again by the Justice Department (DOJ) for allegedly disclosing sensitive national defense information in 2016, according to newly unsealed court documents . items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - As voters prepare to head to the polls for the midterm elections, a conflicting economic sentiment is once again emerging on the campaign trail. “Voters reflect the perception of the cost of living as they experienced, as opposed to what is in the data,” said Alessandro Rebucci, an economics professor at Johns Hopkins Carey Business School. “In the data, you have an economy that is very strong as a whole. items.t: Kentucky joins 33 other states in settlement with crypto kiosk operator
items.x: FRANKFORT, Ky. (WKYT) - Gov. Andy Beshear announced Wednesday that Kentucky has joined 33 other states in a $2.5 million settlement with Coin-Me, a cryptocurrency money transmitter and kiosk operator. Kentucky’s share of the settlement is just under $63,000. The company is accused of violating anti-money laundering and bank secrecy laws. The laws are designed to stop criminals from moving money. Under the settlement, Coin-Me must hire an independent consultant to fix its compliance program. The company also must shut down its virtual currency kiosks by Jan. 1 or face another $4 million in penalties.

items.x: POWELL COUNTY, Ky. (WKYT) - Powell County Schools said late Wednesday that it is investigating a security threat at the district’s high school. After district officials gathered information and reviewed video footage, the student who allegedly made the comment was identified. The student denied any wrongdoing when confronted by district officials, but has been asked to stay home pending an investigation by local law enforcement. items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election

items.t: UK sues CVS in federal court, alleges company owes it millions of dollars
items.x: LEXINGTON, Ky. (WKYT) - The University of Kentucky has sued CVS Health Corporation in United States federal court, according to a report by the Lexington Herald-Leader . The suit, which was filed on Tuesday, accuses CVS and its subsidiary companies of civil racketeering, fraud and breach of contract. The university claims in the suit that the company diverted around $41 million in 340B prescription revenue that was supposed to go to its pharmacies over a five-year period, according to the Herald-Leader. The 310B program allows hospitals to buy drugs at prorated rates and then use the savings to assist patients with the cost of care. UK is asking for damages under the RICO Act. CVS has yet to respond to the suit.

Curtis James Spears, 26, was arrested at approximately 2:13 p.m. on Sunday by the KSP Electronic Crime Branch following an undercover Internet Crimes Against Children investigation. Investigators say the investigation began after discovering Spears sharing images of child sexual exploitation online. A search warrant was executed at a Corbin home, and equipment used to conduct the crime was confiscated and taken to KSP’s forensic laboratory for examination. items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. items.t: VIDEO: Person throws box of cockroaches at Toledo library staff member, prompting temporary closure
items.x: TOLEDO, Ohio (WTVG) - A cockroach attack forced the closure of a Toledo library Tuesday. 13 Action News received the surveillance footage of the incident on Wednesday, included in the video attached at the end of this article. There is no audio. A spokesperson for the Toledo Lucas County Public Library said someone threw a box of cockroaches at a staff member at the Kent Branch Library on Collingwood Blvd on Oct. 27. It’s unclear what led up to the cockroach attack. The branch went into restricted access, then closed for the rest of the day for cleanup and remediation. It reopened on Wednesday. It’s unclear at this time whether anyone will be charged. The investigation is ongoing. Surveillance footage from the Kent Branch Library in Toledo shows someone throwing a box of cockroaches at a library employee on Oct. 27, 2026. items.t: Missing 7-year-old, pregnant mother both found safe
items.x: OVERLAND, Mo. ( KMOV /Gray News) — Officials in Missouri said a missing 7-year-old boy and his pregnant mother were found safe Wednesday. The Missouri State Highway Patrol previously issued an Endangered Person Advisory for Dylan Fernando Zendejas-Gonzalez, 7. Dylan was last seen leaving his home in Overland, near St. Louis, with his mother, Maria Guadalupe Gonzalez-Sanchez, 28. The two were last seen around 1:30 p.m. Sunday. Officials were concerned after personal belongings were left behind at their home. On Wednesday, the Overland Police Department said in a Facebook post that the two were found safe.

Crews spend the summer off-season breaking down the trucks, checking brakes and cleaning up. If passed, in-person voters must show unexpired photo ID: Ohio driver’s license or state ID, U.S. passport or passport card, or military ID from the Ohio National Guard, the U.S. military or the VA. items.t: Some packaged salads recalled for undeclared allergens
items.x: (Gray News) - Packaged salads produced by Taylor Farms have been recalled due to an undeclared allergen. According to the Food and Drug Administration, Taylor Farms is recalling its H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad because it may contain undeclared soy and tree nuts, specifically almonds. “People who have sensitivity or allergy to soy and tree nuts (almonds) may be at risk of a serious adverse reaction if they consume this product,” an FDA press release said. So far there have not been any illnesses or “adverse reactions” reported in connection with the recall. The salads were sold in H-E-B stores across Texas. They can be identified by their UPC code, 041220300457, and their best-by date, Oct. 30, 2026. Customers are asked not to eat the recalled salads and to throw them away or return them to the store for a refund.

items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. Weil said the more skilled the service, the higher the price. “If you need someone to come in and help you prepare food, that’s less expensive than if you need someone to come in and provide nursing-level care,”

items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( InvestigateTV ) - Kids sleeping in shelters, bussed between hotels, and overnights in office buildings. That’s the reality for many foster children in America. items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election

items.x: (Gray News) - Packaged salads produced by Taylor Farms have been recalled due to an undeclared allergen. According to the Food and Drug Administration, Taylor Farms is recalling its H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad because it may contain undeclared soy and tree nuts, specifically almonds. “People who have sensitivity or allergy to soy and tree nuts (almonds) may be at risk of a serious adverse reaction if they consume this product,” an FDA press release said. items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. Weil said the more skilled the service, the higher the price. “If you need someone to come in and help you prepare food, that’s less expensive than if you need someone to come in and provide nursing-level care,”

items.t: New ethanol plant underway near Glen Ullin
items.x: GLEN ULLIN, N.D. (KFYR) - A major development worth hundreds of millions of dollars could bring new jobs and economic opportunities to a small town in North Dakota. Rough Rider Energy is planning an estimated $800 million ethanol production facility a mile east of Glen Ullin. “The Glen Ullin site here was an attractive location because of its proximity to existing infrastructure,” said Wade Boeshans, president of BNI Energy. It’s close to the BNSF rail line, an intersection for three major natural gas lines, and good access to the interstate system. The facility is expected to produce up to 240 million gallons of ethanol each year. It’ll consume about 80 million bushels of corn annually. That production could create another potential market for farmers. The plant’s developers also anticipate approximately 80 permanent jobs with more additional work expected during construction. items.t: Public comment open on proposed pig iron plant for Minot
items.x: MINOT, N.D. (KMOT) - Earlier this year, a pig iron plant was proposed for Northeast Minot. The public now has the chance to comment on the project’s proposed air quality permit. items.t: Midco announces new CEO
items.x: SIOUX FALLS, S.D (KFYR) - Midco announced a new CEO on Tuesday. Pat McAdaragh, the current CEO, will retire on March 1. He served in this role for 46 years. After his retirement, McAdaragh will serve as chair and president of Midcontinent Media, Inc. McAdaragh will be replaced by Ben Dold, who currently serves as Midco’s president and chief operating officer.

items.t: Hawley man turns backyard shed into full-motion racing simulator, hopes to bring concept to Fargo
items.x: HAWLEY, Minn. (Valley News Live) - A Hawley man has turned his backyard shed into a full racing simulator, and now he’s hoping to bring that passion to Fargo. Mitchell Dahlen, founder of MM Simulations, started sim racing after breaking his ankle. When he looked for better equipment, he says the price stood out most. “It started as a, I wanted one of these type of a thing, but when I looked at the price tag, I didn’t want to pay the price tag,” Dahlen said. So he took the wheel on his own project and built it himself. “What you have here is a 150 millimeter actuated with 750-watt servo motors producing close to 400 millimeters per second movement,” Dahlen said. items.t: We compared AI travel videos with real listings; here’s what we found
items.x: ATLANTA, Ga. ( InvestigateTV ) — A scroll through social media can make a mountain cabin, beachfront rental or luxury resort look like an easy escape. But some AI-generated travel videos may not accurately show the property a viewer would book or the price a viewer would pay. We reviewed TikTok posts promoting real hotels, resorts and vacation rentals. The posts included TikTok labels stating they were generated with artificial intelligence and that the creator earns commission. Several directed viewers to major booking services, including Expedia and Booking.com . In multiple examples, the apparently AI-generated video did not appear to match the property’s official listing or other photos. In others, the price promoted in the video was not a deal we could locate when we checked the listing. Using AI to create travel posts is not inherently illegal. items.t: Missing woman reportedly found alive in Mexico, but her family has doubts
items.x: PHOENIX ( KPHO /Gray News) — Mexican authorities said a missing Arizona woman was believed to have been found in Tijuana, but family members say they have doubts. Shayna Feinman, 35, was reported missing in March 2024. A Tijuana security force said Feinman was found on Oct. 23 after reports of a woman matching her description in an Encino neighborhood. The security force said the woman was confirmed to be Feinman, but Yavapai County Sheriff’s Office officials initially said they couldn’t independently confirm her identity because of “insufficient evidence.” Feinman’s sister Kara added that she did not recognize the person in Mexico and didn’t have hard evidence that the person was indeed her sister. Kara said this wasn’t the first time Feinman was reported to have been spotted. Feinman’s sister called these types of reports with little evidence from law enforcement agencies disheartening

items.t: Zebra Mussels discovered in Lake Sakakawea
items.x: LAKE SAKAKAWEA N.D. (KFYR) - North Dakota Game and Fish have confirmed the presence of Zebra Mussel in Lake Sakakawea. The invasive mussel was found in the easternmost portion of the man-made lake during routine sampling. Current findings suggest the mussel infestation is isolated. More sampling will be done to decide how far the mussels have spread. Falling water temperatures will help reduce the immediate spread of Zebra Mussels, officials note.

items.t: Special needs teacher accused of pouring hot sauce on student’s tongue as a punishment
items.x: HOUSTON COUNTY, Ala. ( WTVY /Gray News) - An Alabama special needs teacher is facing child abuse charges after deputies say she poured hot sauce on a student’s tongue. Heather Varner Hunter, a 46-year-old special needs teacher at Cottonwood Elementary School, allegedly used hot sauce to punish a student for sticking out their tongue in September. A Houston County Sheriff’s Office investigation followed. Jail records show Hunter was arrested Monday afternoon. She is no longer employed by the Houston County School System, according to Superintendent Brandy White. White said the school system cooperated fully with authorities, and all information has been turned over to the Alabama Department of Human Resources. items.t: Former true-crime producer accused of posing as aircraft heiress added to FBI most-wanted list
items.x: (Gray News) - A 75-year-old woman who allegedly posed as an heiress to steal more than $14 million has been added to the FBI’s Most Wanted list. According to the FBI, Mary Carole McDonnell is accused of posing as the heiress to the McDonnell Aircraft family with an $80 million secret trust. The McDonnell Aircraft Corporation was an aerospace manufacturer best known for its military aircrafts. The FBI said the alleged scheme began in July 2017 and lasted until May 2018. McDonnell allegedly obtained $14.7 million from Banc of California, as well as an additional $15 million from other financial institutions. On Dec. 12, 2018, a federal arrest warrant was issued for McDonnell. She faces charges of bank fraud and aggravated identity theft. McDonnell is described as 5-foot-7 with blond hair and blue eyes. items.t: Secretary Doug Burgum signs order to support ranchers
items.x: WASHINGTON (KFYR) - Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum signed an order expanding grazing opportunities for ranchers on Tuesday. It establishes a Rangeland Health Initiative, which prioritizes the health of rangeland to be used by livestock. The Initiative Lead, who has yet to be named, will report within 180 days on the amount and health of unused grazing land that can be opened for ranchers. The permit process for the grazing of unused lands will be expedited, and ranchers will have these permits for 10 years. The Bureau of Land Management (BLM) must report on the backlog of permits, and its goal to eliminate this backlog. To better preserve rangeland, BLM is working with other state and federal agencies to ensure the supply of native seeds is matching the demand. items.t: Aging Untold: Hospice doesn’t have to happen at home
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — On this episode of Aging Untold, we explore compassionate hospice care options beyond the home, focusing on comfort, dignity and family support. Plus, we share practical advice for older adults stepping up to raise school-aged kids and navigating today’s modern classrooms. Then, a breast cancer survivor opens up about the emotional toll of chemotherapy-induced hair loss and how she reclaimed her identity and strength. Hospice doesn’t have to happen at home Hospice care is about comfort, dignity and quality of life. It isn’t tied to one setting, the Aging Untold experts said. items.t: The Exoneree Band: How a group of wrongfully convicted men found their voice through music
items.x: ( Aging Untold )— They don’t have the fame of The Beatles or the fortune of The Rolling Stones, but the members of The Exoneree band share something far more profound. Now, as free men, they are using the power of music to heal, to tell their stories, and to build a brotherhood unlike any other. The band was born out of the Innocence Network’s annual conference, a gathering that brings together wrongfully convicted people from across the country. In 2011, this group of musically inclined exonerees found each other, and what started as a jam session quickly turned into something more. “It turned into a really nice brotherhood of guys who were not only musicians but had went through the same thing of being wrongfully convicted,” one band member recalls. items.t: ‘McMillan & Wife’ actress Susan Saint James dies at 80
items.x: (Gray News) - Emmy-winning actress Susan Saint James has died. She was 80 years old. Saint James, who starred in “McMillan & Wife,” “Kate & Allie” and “The Name Game,” died Monday after being diagnosed with pancreatic cancer, according to People . Her family said she was “generous with her time and energy, which she valued more than money, and instinctively drawn to whoever needed lifting up,” in a statement to People. Saint James “never met a stranger” and “taught her children to pause, be kind and look out for other people,” her family said. “Every person she met became the most important person in the room at that moment, from a fellow board member to the clerk at the shoe store, who usually walked away knowing her entire life story,” her family said. items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - With Election Day less than a week away, President Donald Trump is expected to make another campaign stop in Ohio, where two competitive races could have national implications. The president’s visit comes amid growing controversy surrounding Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy, whose campaign released a viral attack ad featuring the estranged mother of his Democratic opponent, Dr. Amy Acton. Acton and her brother were removed from their mother’s custody after Acton’s stepfather was charged with sexually abusing her. “My opponent has chosen to exploit my childhood to save his struggling campaign, but it’s not going to work,” Acton said at recent campaign even. items.t: Breast cancer survivor faced hair loss during chemotherapy and reclaimed her identity
items.x: KANSAS CITY, Mo. ( Aging Untold ) — Hair loss is often the most common and visually striking side effect of chemotherapy, especially for women. Lisa Steinhauser, a breast cancer survivor, said she lost her hair and part of her identity during chemotherapy. Now she inspires patients to find strength during their own battle. Hair as part of her identity “So when I knew I was going to lose my hair, that was pretty hard because I had a lot of it,” she said. Hair has always been Steinhauser’s craft, artistry and expression. Diagnosis and treatment In December 2021, Steinhauser went in for a routine mammogram, and she said doctors found a spot they were concerned about. “I really was not expecting it to be anything at all, but it was,” she said. items.t: How to use AI to budget for the holidays without overspending
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Holiday expenses often extend well beyond gifts and food, and those additional costs can add up quickly. Cherry Dale, vice president of financial education at Virginia Credit Union, said the first step to managing holiday spending is a simple list — before ever opening an AI tool like ChatGPT or Claude. Dale recommends listing everything planned for November and December spending, including travel, decorations, gifts and hosting costs. She said AI can help organize a budget, but personal information such as a name or banking details should never be entered. Dale said general, non-identifying details can still produce a useful, personalized budget. “You can put generic things like, ‘Hey, I’m hosting eight people for Thanksgiving, and I have six adults, two children. I would like to create a traditional Thanksgiving meal. Can you map out a budget for me with all of this

items.t: One dead following shooting in Belcourt
items.x: BELCOURT, N.D. (KFYR) - One person is dead following a shooting in Belcourt. The Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa released a statement confirming the death. Law enforcement says that a suspect is in custody, and there is no known ongoing threat to the community. They say they believe this was an isolated incident, and the investigation remains ongoing. The information from the tribe does not include where or when the shooting may have occurred. We left a message with the Bureau of Indian Affairs to get more information. We’ll update you when we hear back from the agency.

items.t: ND homeowners may see some home insurance rate stabilization after rough years
items.x: BISMARCK, N.D. (KFYR) - Your home insurance bill may finally be cooling off — at least a little. The North Dakota Insurance Department says homeowners saw some rate stabilization in 2026 after several rough years of increases, and officials hope that holds into 2027. Insurance Commissioner Jon Godfread said part of that stabilization comes down to weather, as wind and hail are North Dakota’s biggest insurance threats. “We’ve had a pretty relatively calm storm season, so that should help keep some downward pressure on those rates,” Godfread said. But rebuilding still costs far more than it used to — and that’s what drives premiums up. Godfread said labor costs are up 30% to 40%, along with materials like shingles and lumber. Officers at the Northwest Correctional Complex in Lake County discovered inmate Jacob Morley was missing late Sunday night. Surveillance footage shows Morley breached a perimeter fence and left the facility in his prison uniform. Authorities released video of him allegedly stealing a white 2008 Ford F-350 during his escape around 1 a.m. Monday. The truck has a Tennessee license plate 138BBQV and is marked with Lindamood Planting Company on the side. items.t: U.S. Capitol Christmas Tree to make Black Hills stop in Custer on Nov. 10
items.x: RAPID CITY, S.D. (KOTA) - The U.S. Capitol Christmas Tree is coming to the Black Hills, with a stop planned in Custer on Nov. 10 as the tree makes its way from Idaho to Washington, D.C. The Custer Area Chamber of Commerce will host a community celebration from 4 to 6 p.m. at Way Park in downtown Custer to mark the occasion. The family-friendly event will feature Santa Claus, Smokey Bear, educational displays and merchandise. Visitors also will have a chance to sign a banner that will travel with the tree to the nation’s capital. Local law enforcement, fire department and U.S. Forest Service vehicles are expected to escort the tree into town in a mini parade. Organizers are still determining the route and plan to release more details closer to the event. The tree will eventually be displayed on the West Lawn of the U.S. Capitol in Washington, D.C. Wyle, 55, is the star of the hit HBO show “The Pitt.” He broke onto the scene in the 1990s when he starred as the handsome young Dr. Carter on “ER” alongside George Clooney. items.t: Raising school-aged grandkids: how to handle homework and school in a digital age
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — For some older adults, this chapter of life was supposed to mean retirement. Instead, they are raising school-age kids again, navigating online portals, teacher apps and school meetings that look nothing like the school they remember.
