items.t: Update: Missing 88-year-old found, according to Moorhead police
items.x: MOORHEAD, Minn. (Valley News Live) - Update : Moorhead police says, Dean Fjeld has been located and is safe. Original : Moorhead Police are asking for the public’s help finding an endangered missing adult. Dean Fjeld, 88, who has been diagnosed with dementia and Alzheimer’s disease, left his residence around 9:30 p.m. Monday, Oct. 26. Fjeld is described as 5′11″, 165 pounds, with blue eyes and light brown hair. He was last seen wearing an Excel Energy T-shirt, an older spring beige-colored jacket, blue jeans and tennis shoes. Police say he was driving a 2016 white Ford F-150 with Minnesota plate NYM-325. Anyone with information about his whereabouts is asked to contact Moorhead Police through the Red River Regional Dispatch Center at 701-451-7660.

items.t: Economist explains how the ‘K-shaped economy’ is impacting the midterms
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - As voters prepare to head to the polls for the midterm elections, a conflicting economic sentiment is once again emerging on the campaign trail. “Voters reflect the perception of the cost of living as they experienced, as opposed to what is in the data,” said Alessandro Rebucci, an economics professor at Johns Hopkins Carey Business School. “In the data, you have an economy that is very strong as a whole. Police said as part of the investigation, they found 95 grams of fentanyl, 44.6 grams of methamphetamine, more than $3,745 in cash, two guns, one with an obliterated serial number, a Taser, scales and packaging materials. Jesus David Mendez of Salem was arrested near Center Street Northeast and 12th Street Northeast, according to police. Earlier on Wednesday, police announced that they arrested a 46-year-old man on Monday in connection to an ongoing investigation into drug sales in downtown Salem. items.t: Portland council bans concealed guns in certain city buildings
items.x: PORTLAND Ore. (KPTV) - The Portland City Council on Wednesday approved banning concealed carry handguns in city buildings with 12 votes in favor. The ordinance removes a state-law exception that let people with concealed handgun licenses bring guns into certain public buildings. Oregon lawmakers gave local governments authority to restrict that exception in 2025. The ban applies to three city-owned and managed buildings where official government meetings are held. The city administrator will identify the locations, post signs at entrances and publish the list online. The city will also set up an enforcement process that includes notice and a chance to comply before sending a violation to law enforcement. items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election

items.t: Library says person threw box of cockroaches at a staff member, prompting closure
items.x: TOLEDO, Ohio ( WTVG /Gray News) - A cockroach attack forced the closure of a library in Ohio this week. Surveillance footage was released by the Toledo Lucas County Public Library, appearing to show a person throwing a box of cockroaches at a staff member on Tuesday at the Kent Branch Library. Surveillance footage apparently shows someone throwing a box of cockroaches at a library employee in Ohio. (Source: Toledo Lucas County Public Library) A library spokesperson confirmed the throwing of the box of cockroaches at the library worker on Collingwood Blvd. But it wasn’t immediately shared what led up to the cockroach attack. The library was said to have gone into restricted access before closing for the rest of the day for cleanup and remediation. The Kent Branch Library reopened Wednesday. Officials did not say whether anyone would be facing any charges.

items.t: 8-month-old dies after left alone in running bathtub, police say
items.x: STERLING, Va. (Gray News) - A Virginia woman was arrested after her 8-month-old died after being left unattended in a bathtub, according to authorities. Rosellena Pisani, 30, was arrested and charged with homicide, two counts of child abuse and three counts of child endangerment, a press release said. On Sept. 12, emergency medical personnel and sheriff’s deputies responded to the residence after receiving a call about an unresponsive infant. Investigators determined the baby had been left unsupervised in a bathtub with the water running. Three children, ranging in age from 8 months to 8 years old, were at home during the incident, according to police. Loudoun County Sheriff Mike Chapman called the baby’s death heartbreaking, saying caregivers have a fundamental duty to protect children. He added investigators remain committed to seeking justice in the case.

items.t: Some packaged salads recalled for undeclared allergens
items.x: (Gray News) - Packaged salads produced by Taylor Farms have been recalled due to an undeclared allergen. According to the Food and Drug Administration, Taylor Farms is recalling its H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad because it may contain undeclared soy and tree nuts, specifically almonds. “People who have sensitivity or allergy to soy and tree nuts (almonds) may be at risk of a serious adverse reaction if they consume this product,” an FDA press release said. So far there have not been any illnesses or “adverse reactions” reported in connection with the recall. The salads were sold in H-E-B stores across Texas. They can be identified by their UPC code, 041220300457, and their best-by date, Oct. 30, 2026. Customers are asked not to eat the recalled salads and to throw them away or return them to the store for a refund.

items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. Weil said the more skilled the service, the higher the price. “If you need someone to come in and help you prepare food, that’s less expensive than if you need someone to come in and provide nursing-level care,”

items.t: Police arrest man accused of selling meth to homeless people in Salem
items.x: SALEM, Ore. (KPTV) - A 46-year-old man is facing several charges following an investigation into methamphetamine sales in downtown Salem, according to police. Police say Engels A. Marcelino sold meth to homeless people in Wallace Marine Park and the downtown area. Detectives learned he intended to sell meth at Riverfront Park as well. On Monday, Oct. 26, officers tried to stop Marcelino at the park, but he ran from them. He was taken into custody after a short foot pursuit. According to police, detectives found a loaded handgun, 59.7 grams of methamphetamine, and $233 in cash in Marcelino’s bag. Marcelino was booked into the Marion County Jail for unlawful delivery of methamphetamine, unlawful possession of methamphetamine, and felon in possession of a firearm. The investigation is ongoing, and no other details have been released at this time.

items.t: Butter sold in 10 states recalled over possible yeast, mold and E. coli contamination
items.x: (Gray News) - Butter is being recalled because it might be contaminated with yeast, mold and E. coli, according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. More than 1,300 cases of Miyoko’s Creamery European Style Salted Plant Milk Butter have been recalled in Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, New Jersey, New Hampshire and Wisconsin. The recalled butter has lot code 07871 and a best-by date of Nov. 5, 2026. If you have the butter, you should not eat it, but the recall notice did not give further information about refunds.

items.t: New permanent homeless shelter pod village opens in Aloha
items.x: ALOHA Ore. (KPTV) - Washington County officials celebrated the official opening of a permanent homeless shelter pod village on Tuesday. Next Step Community features 60 pallet-style homes that can accommodate up to 70 people. The county purchased the site at 3390 Southwest 209th Avenue in Aloha last December, in order to relocate a temporary pod village into a permanent shelter. Lisa Steinhauser, a breast cancer survivor, said she lost her hair and part of her identity during chemotherapy. Now she inspires patients to find strength during their own battle. Diagnosis and treatment In December 2021, Steinhauser went in for a routine mammogram, and she said doctors found a spot they were concerned about. “I really was not expecting it to be anything at all, but it was,” she said. items.t: How to use AI to budget for the holidays without overspending
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Holiday expenses often extend well beyond gifts and food, and those additional costs can add up quickly. Cherry Dale, vice president of financial education at Virginia Credit Union, said the first step to managing holiday spending is a simple list — before ever opening an AI tool like ChatGPT or Claude. Dale recommends listing everything planned for November and December spending, including travel, decorations, gifts and hosting costs. She said AI can help organize a budget, but personal information such as a name or banking details should never be entered. Dale said general, non-identifying details can still produce a useful, personalized budget. “You can put generic things like, ‘Hey, I’m hosting eight people for Thanksgiving, and I have six adults, two children. Surveillance footage shows Morley breached a perimeter fence and left the facility in his prison uniform. Authorities released video of him allegedly stealing a white 2008 Ford F-350 during his escape around 1 a.m. Monday. The truck has a Tennessee license plate 138BBQV and is marked with Lindamood Planting Company on the side. items.t: Tigard-Tualatin district to close elementary school in 2028
items.x: TIGARD, Ore. (KPTV) - The Tigard-Tualatin School District plans to close an elementary school at the start of the 2028-29 school year, according to the district. The district has not specified which school will close. The district said the closure is due to a decline in enrollment, primarily caused by low birth rates. According to the district, the school that will be closed will be based on student enrollment, the number of students and boundaries that would be affected, and predicted growth in the neighborhood. This comes as Portland Public Schools is looking to close as many as 14 schools and Salem-Keizer is expecting to close six elementary schools starting next school year. Several other districts in Oregon are also planning to close some schools. Most of them cite declining enrollment due to low birth rates.

items.t: Rosewood Initiative builds ‘food forest’ to address child hunger in Portland
items.x: PORTLAND, Ore. (KPTV) - One in five children in Oregon and southwest Washington is facing food insecurity, according to the report. Community organizations are using a variety of strategies to address the problem, including a “food forest” being built in southeast Portland. The Rosewood Initiative held a fall harvest festival to celebrate progress on the project. Not all the food at the event was grown on site. “Sundays I think they’re the biggest days where families can really come and just either harvest the fruits and vegetables that are here or plant new ones for next season,” Mary Byrd, a Rosewood Initiative representative said. Mary Byrd has lived in Portland’s Rosewood neighborhood for 17 years and raised her three children there. “When they were little we didn’t have any parks really. We had to go all the way down to 17th – no community gardens, no community centers,” Byrd said.

items.t: Fire damages garage in NE Portland, cat rescued
items.x: PORTLAND, Ore. (KPTV) - A fire damaged a garage in northeast Portland early Tuesday morning. Just before 4 a.m., Portland Fire & Rescue crews responded to a house fire near Northeast San Rafael Street and Northeast 122nd Avenue. The first crews on scene found heavy fire, with flames burning close to overhead power lines. Everyone inside the home made it out safely before crews arrived. One cat was rescued by firefighters. PF&R said there were two cats that did not survive the fire. The garage sustained heavy damage, and a window of the home was blown out from the heat. There were no injuries reported. Investigators determined the cause of the fire was lithium ion batteries, according to PF&R.

items.t: ‘You can’t go any higher’: American Airlines’ most senior flight attendant retires
items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. (Gray News) - American Airlines’ most senior flight attendant is retiring after nearly 64 years with the company. Carol Fair has worked as a flight attendant for 63 years. At 83, she is retiring at the top of American Airlines’ seniority list. “It’s time. I’ve enjoyed every minute of it. I made No. 1 out of 30,000. You can’t go any higher, so I might as well hang it up,” Fair said in an interview with Forbes . Her last trip was on an American Airlines flight from London to Charlotte, North Carolina, on Monday. A crowd celebrated Fair when the plane landed at Charlotte Douglas International Airport. Fair is a 2008 inductee of the North Carolina Transportation Hall of Fame and is also a member of the Tennessee Aviation Hall of Fame. Her career is also featured in an exhibit at the Sullenberger Aviation Museum.

items.x: COLUMBIA, S.C. (WIS) - The biggest concern at Harvest Hope Food Bank as the holidays approach is whether there will be enough food to fill its shelves. Harvest Hope Food Bank CEO Sy Hughes said the need for free food services is growing, with the organization serving a large number of households. “We’re serving about just under 200,000 households across the state,” Hughes said. The food bank’s reach extends across 20 counties. Hughes said the food bank has calculated a 40% year-over-year increase in families facing food insecurity. In the Midlands, the food bank serves an average of 18,000 people per month through emergency shelter and food bank initiatives. Officials also said food insecurity has risen from affecting 1 in 7 people to 1 in 6. “Which is kind of staggering when you think about it. items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election

Surveillance footage apparently shows someone throwing a box of cockroaches at a library employee in Ohio. (Source: Toledo Lucas County Public Library) A library spokesperson confirmed the throwing of the box of cockroaches at the library worker on Collingwood Blvd. But it wasn’t immediately shared what led up to the cockroach attack. The library was said to have gone into restricted access before closing for the rest of the day for cleanup and remediation. The Kent Branch Library reopened Wednesday. Officials did not say whether anyone would be facing any charges.

items.x: MADISONVILLE, Ky. ( WFIE /Gray News) — A Kentucky doctor who accidentally left her grandchild unattended in a hot car for about eight hours will not be indicted for the baby’s death. Madisonville police said 10-month-old Scottie Crowell died in August . On Tuesday, a grand jury found there was insufficient probable cause for an indictment. Police said Scottie’s grandmother picked her up in the morning of Aug. 13 and was supposed to take her to daycare. She forgot the child was in the car and went to work, police said. She arrived at Owensboro Health Multi-Care, where she works as a doctor, around 8 a.m. The baby’s father called his wife after trying to pick up Scottie from daycare, but the child was not there. items.t: Widow searches for lost wedding ring when husband dies 3 days after getting married in Las Vegas
items.x: LAS VEGAS ( KVVU /Gray News) — A South Dakota woman is asking for help finding the wedding ring her husband lost in Las Vegas the night they married. Tammy Bishop and Will Mulroy were married Oct. 20 at the Viva Las Vegas Chapel. Bishop said they celebrated on a party bus and toured the Strip. At a bar, though, she says Mulroy looked down and realized his ring was gone. “We got to a bar. He looked down and his band was gone. He lost it. He started crying,” Bishop said. According to Bishop, he told her the ring was two sizes too big because he had lost weight. She said the ring may have slid off on the bus or while he moved into his wheelchair. It may also have come off while he rolled down the Strip. “We backtracked our steps. We told the bus driver. We had everyone looking. We couldn’t find it,” she said. items.t: Midlands woman sentenced for deadly pedestrian crash
items.x: COLUMBIA, S.C. (WIS) - A woman received her sentence on Wednesday for killing a pedestrian while speeding. According to the Columbia Police Department, Madeline Kuester drove 88 miles per hour along a road with a 35 miles per hour speed limit on June 18, 2024. She hit a pedestrian, identified as Charlton Ard, who traveled 250 feet after being hit by the vehicle and died. The crash occurred at the 1900 block of Rosewood Drive. Columbia Police said Kuester turned herself in. Kuester pled guilty on one count of reckless homicide. No drugs or alcohol were involved in the incident. Her defense argued for rehabilitation instead of a long prison sentence due to her age and criminal history. Kuester, who was 18-years-old during in the incident, had just graduated high school and planned to attend Clemson University. items.t: ‘I miss her like crazy’: Loved ones remembering post office worker hit and killed by car
items.x: FORT THOMAS, Ky. ( WXIX /Gray News) - Loved ones and a Kentucky community are mourning a post office worker who was hit and killed by a car while walking earlier this month. Marchelle Bertram worked at the front desk of the Fort Thomas Post Office for years, helping people who came in. Sadly, she lost her life in a collision in Bellevue on Oct. 15. Her daughter, Whitney Bertram, said she is remembering her mother while seeing a large amount of support from the community following her death. “There are so many people I don’t know whose lives she’s touched and affected,” Whitney Bertram said. The crash occurred while Marchelle Bertram was walking on Memorial Parkway near her home. Her daughter said she rushed to the hospital after learning her mother had been hit by a vehicle. “Given the grave amount of injuries she sustained, there was no way she was going to survive,” she said. items.t: Georgia man sentenced 25 years in South Carolina prison for drug trafficking
items.x: LEXINGTON, S.C. (WIS) - A man from Augusta was convicted by a Lexington County jury this month for trafficking methamphetamine. A judge sentenced Angelo Allen, 41, to 25 years in the South Carolina Department of Corrections on Oct. 8. According to Eleventh Circuit Solicitor Rick Hubbard, Allen’s sentence is the minimum for his offense. Allen was pulled over on I-20 in Lexington County while he was traveling from Augusta to Lexington on March 12, 2025. Law enforcement found 491 grams of methamphetamine in the vehicle under the passenger seat. Allen was the only person in the vehicle, and the vehicle was registered in his name. The jury heard Allen say in his testimony that he was traveling from Georgia to Lexington County for a drug transaction, Hubbard said. items.x: (Gray News) - Ernie Johnson announced he will be stepping down as host of “Inside the NBA” at the end of the season. The Sports Broadcasting Hall of Famer took to social media on Wednesday to explain his decision to step away, saying, “It’s just time.” Johnson, 70, stated that he would not be retiring, but cutting back. “This is by no means the end. It’s just a turning of the page,” Johnson said. “And I’ll forever cherish every chapter we have written with ‘Inside the NBA.’” Johnson said he plans to continue to work, including covering the NCAA men’s basketball tournament for CBS and Turner Sports. The six-time Sports Emmy Award winner acknowledged that he has dealt with heart issues in recent years, but that isn’t the reason he’s stepping away from the show. “I just want to slow down a bit,” he added in his social media post. items.t: Police department closes its investigation into Hayden Panettiere’s death
items.x: GREENVILLE, S.C. ( WHNS /Gray News) - The Greenville Police Department said it has officially closed its investigation into the death of Hayden Panettiere. Police said Panettiere’s death has been ruled accidental based on the medical examiner’s determination and the findings of the investigation. Panettiere, 36, died from an accidental overdose involving multiple prescription medications and fentanyl, according to findings previously released by the Greenville County Coroner’s Office. Toxicology testing determined the cause of death to be the toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, alprazolam, methocarbamol and quetiapine. An autopsy showed no signs of contributing trauma. On Aug. 16, Panettiere was found unresponsive inside an apartment in Greenville, where she had been temporarily staying. items.x: SCOTTSDALE, Ariz. ( KPHO /Gray News) - A man lost thousands of dollars after getting a call that appeared to come from his father’s phone number, with a stranger claiming his parents were being held at gunpoint. Curtis Indyke was asleep around 11:30 p.m. on Oct. 21 when he got a call that appeared to be from his dad, who lives in Virginia. Indyke lives in Arizona. “I answer the phone and it’s not my dad. It’s some other male saying he has my parents basically at gunpoint,” Indyke said. The caller told him to pay or his parents would be shot. While still on the phone, Indyke said he texted 911 to report his parents were being held hostage in Virginia. The person who claimed to be holding Indyke’s parents hostage continued making threats. items.t: 8-month-old dies after left alone in running bathtub, police say
items.x: STERLING, Va. (Gray News) - A Virginia woman was arrested after her 8-month-old died after being left unattended in a bathtub, according to authorities. Rosellena Pisani, 30, was arrested and charged with homicide, two counts of child abuse and three counts of child endangerment, a press release said. On Sept. 12, emergency medical personnel and sheriff’s deputies responded to the residence after receiving a call about an unresponsive infant. Investigators determined the baby had been left unsupervised in a bathtub with the water running. Three children, ranging in age from 8 months to 8 years old, were at home during the incident, according to police. Loudoun County Sheriff Mike Chapman called the baby’s death heartbreaking, saying caregivers have a fundamental duty to protect children. He added investigators remain committed to seeking justice in the case.

items.t: Missing 7-year-old, pregnant mother both found safe
items.x: OVERLAND, Mo. ( KMOV /Gray News) — Officials in Missouri said a missing 7-year-old boy and his pregnant mother were found safe Wednesday. The Missouri State Highway Patrol previously issued an Endangered Person Advisory for Dylan Fernando Zendejas-Gonzalez, 7. Dylan was last seen leaving his home in Overland, near St. Louis, with his mother, Maria Guadalupe Gonzalez-Sanchez, 28. The two were last seen around 1:30 p.m. Sunday. Officials were concerned after personal belongings were left behind at their home. On Wednesday, the Overland Police Department said in a Facebook post that the two were found safe.

items.x: COLUMBIA, S.C. (WIS) - South Carolina is seeing record turnout for early voting a little over a week into the window. Data from the South Carolina Election Commission shows that 84,029 votes were cast on Tuesday, bringing the statewide total to 671,314. items.t: Some packaged salads recalled for undeclared allergens
items.x: (Gray News) - Packaged salads produced by Taylor Farms have been recalled due to an undeclared allergen. According to the Food and Drug Administration, Taylor Farms is recalling its H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad because it may contain undeclared soy and tree nuts, specifically almonds. “People who have sensitivity or allergy to soy and tree nuts (almonds) may be at risk of a serious adverse reaction if they consume this product,” an FDA press release said. So far there have not been any illnesses or “adverse reactions” reported in connection with the recall. The salads were sold in H-E-B stores across Texas. They can be identified by their UPC code, 041220300457, and their best-by date, Oct. 30, 2026. Customers are asked not to eat the recalled salads and to throw them away or return them to the store for a refund.

items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. Weil said the more skilled the service, the higher the price. “If you need someone to come in and help you prepare food, that’s less expensive than if you need someone to come in and provide nursing-level care,”

items.t: She was born with eight fingers on one hand. Her family traveled to America for the surgery
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - A family traveled from Turkey to St. Louis for their daughter’s surgery to treat a rare condition affecting fewer than 100 people worldwide. Elisa, an 18-month-old, was born with eight fingers on her left hand. She was diagnosed with Ulnar Dimelia, also known as Mirror Hand Syndrome. “Mirror Hand is incredibly uncommon, and even surgeons like myself who take care of a great deal of kids almost never see this in their career. So, it’s really uncommon. Numbers are hard to come by, but one in a million or less is probably about right,” said Dr. Charles Goldfarb, Chief of Orthopedic Surgery at St. Louis Children’s Hospital. The condition leaves patients without a radius bone. items.t: Officials working to expand foster care for children in America, here’s how
items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( InvestigateTV ) - Kids sleeping in shelters, bussed between hotels, and overnights in office buildings. That’s the reality for many foster children in America. Guyton says she has seen children begin dating as early as elementary school, making it important for parents to start conversations about healthy relationships at a young age. items.x: WEST COLUMBIA, S.C. (WIS) - Community volunteers joined Lowe’s Red Vest associates to renovate and restore Growing Hope’s Supportive Transitional Living Apartments. The program helps young people who have aged out of the foster care system have a place to call home. items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election

items.t: Library says person threw box of cockroaches at a staff member, prompting closure
items.x: TOLEDO, Ohio ( WTVG /Gray News) - A cockroach attack forced the closure of a library in Ohio this week. Surveillance footage was released by the Toledo Lucas County Public Library, appearing to show a person throwing a box of cockroaches at a staff member on Tuesday at the Kent Branch Library. Surveillance footage apparently shows someone throwing a box of cockroaches at a library employee in Ohio. (Source: Toledo Lucas County Public Library) A library spokesperson confirmed the throwing of the box of cockroaches at the library worker on Collingwood Blvd. But it wasn’t immediately shared what led up to the cockroach attack. The library was said to have gone into restricted access before closing for the rest of the day for cleanup and remediation. The Kent Branch Library reopened Wednesday. Officials did not say whether anyone would be facing any charges.

items.t: 8-month-old dies after left alone in running bathtub, police say
items.x: STERLING, Va. (Gray News) - A Virginia woman was arrested after her 8-month-old died after being left unattended in a bathtub, according to authorities. Rosellena Pisani, 30, was arrested and charged with homicide, two counts of child abuse and three counts of child endangerment, a press release said. On Sept. 12, emergency medical personnel and sheriff’s deputies responded to the residence after receiving a call about an unresponsive infant. Investigators determined the baby had been left unsupervised in a bathtub with the water running. Three children, ranging in age from 8 months to 8 years old, were at home during the incident, according to police. Loudoun County Sheriff Mike Chapman called the baby’s death heartbreaking, saying caregivers have a fundamental duty to protect children. He added investigators remain committed to seeking justice in the case.

items.t: Missing 7-year-old, pregnant mother both found safe
items.x: OVERLAND, Mo. ( KMOV /Gray News) — Officials in Missouri said a missing 7-year-old boy and his pregnant mother were found safe Wednesday. The Missouri State Highway Patrol previously issued an Endangered Person Advisory for Dylan Fernando Zendejas-Gonzalez, 7. Dylan was last seen leaving his home in Overland, near St. Louis, with his mother, Maria Guadalupe Gonzalez-Sanchez, 28. The two were last seen around 1:30 p.m. Sunday. Officials were concerned after personal belongings were left behind at their home. On Wednesday, the Overland Police Department said in a Facebook post that the two were found safe.

items.t: Some Monroe County schools placed on modified lockdown
items.x: PETERSTOWN, W.Va. (WVVA) - Some Monroe County schools have been partially locked down as the result of a situation in a neighboring county. Superintendent Jason Conaway said the district’s Peterstown complex and James Monroe High School have been placed on a modified lockdown due to a situation in neighboring Giles County. Conaway was unable to provide information about the situation in Giles County. WVVA reached out to Giles County schools and an official said the situation does not involve one of the district’s schools. WVVA also reached out to the Giles County Sheriff’s Office and an official declined to comment, citing a policy of not providing information to media members. This story is breaking news and will be updated as more information becomes available.

items.t: Meet the volunteers who bring flowers from weddings and funerals to hospice patients
items.x: LOUISVILLE, Ky. ( Aging Untold ) — Inside Crescent Hill Baptist Church in Louisville, a group of volunteers gathers each week surrounded by color, creativity and collaboration. They call themselves the Flower Buds. From events to those in need The Flower Buds take donated flowers from weddings, funerals, wholesalers, supermarkets, florists, galas, banquets and other community events. They cut, clean and arrange the blooms into vases, then deliver them to nursing homes, the VA hospital, assisted living facilities and shelters. “Amazingly gifted with so many flowers from places like Kroger who have overbought and can’t sell them, and they allow us to pick them up and then bring them here, and then we cut them, clean them and vase them. items.t: Some packaged salads recalled for undeclared allergens
items.x: (Gray News) - Packaged salads produced by Taylor Farms have been recalled due to an undeclared allergen. According to the Food and Drug Administration, Taylor Farms is recalling its H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad because it may contain undeclared soy and tree nuts, specifically almonds. “People who have sensitivity or allergy to soy and tree nuts (almonds) may be at risk of a serious adverse reaction if they consume this product,” an FDA press release said. So far there have not been any illnesses or “adverse reactions” reported in connection with the recall. The salads were sold in H-E-B stores across Texas. They can be identified by their UPC code, 041220300457, and their best-by date, Oct. 30, 2026. Customers are asked not to eat the recalled salads and to throw them away or return them to the store for a refund.

items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — More than 60 million Americans are family caregivers, balancing work, kids and care for an aging parent or loved one. Jason Resendez, president and CEO of the National Alliance for Caregiving, recently testified before the U.S. Senate Special Committee on Aging. He joined gerontologist “Sam” Cradduck to talk through the solutions he presented. The three policies he brought to lawmakers Resendez said the National Alliance for Caregiving is championing changes “to address so many of the pain points that family caregivers face every day.” 1) Older Americans Act funding He said one priority is reauthorization and funding of the Older Americans Act. Resendez said the law provides dollars for state Area Agencies on Aging to deliver services for older adults, such as Meals on Wheels and caregiver support. “One of the only federal line items for caregiving comes through the Ol

items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. Weil said the more skilled the service, the higher the price. “If you need someone to come in and help you prepare food, that’s less expensive than if you need someone to come in and provide nursing-level care,”

items.t: Butter sold in 10 states recalled over possible yeast, mold and E. coli contamination
items.x: (Gray News) - Butter is being recalled because it might be contaminated with yeast, mold and E. coli, according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. More than 1,300 cases of Miyoko’s Creamery European Style Salted Plant Milk Butter have been recalled in Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Iowa, Illinois, Indiana, Maryland, New Jersey, New Hampshire and Wisconsin. The recalled butter has lot code 07871 and a best-by date of Nov. 5, 2026. If you have the butter, you should not eat it, but the recall notice did not give further information about refunds.

items.t: She was born with eight fingers on one hand. Her family traveled to America for the surgery
items.x: ST. LOUIS, Mo. ( InvestigateTV ) - A family traveled from Turkey to St. Louis for their daughter’s surgery to treat a rare condition affecting fewer than 100 people worldwide. Elisa, an 18-month-old, was born with eight fingers on her left hand. She was diagnosed with Ulnar Dimelia, also known as Mirror Hand Syndrome. “Mirror Hand is incredibly uncommon, and even surgeons like myself who take care of a great deal of kids almost never see this in their career. So, it’s really uncommon. Numbers are hard to come by, but one in a million or less is probably about right,” said Dr. Charles Goldfarb, Chief of Orthopedic Surgery at St. Louis Children’s Hospital. The condition leaves patients without a radius bone. items.x: NASHVILLE, Tenn. ( InvestigateTV ) - Kids sleeping in shelters, bussed between hotels, and overnights in office buildings. That’s the reality for many foster children in America. items.x: BLUEFIELD, W.Va. (WVVA) - Changes could be made to a Bluefield holiday tradition this year. The city is considering changes to the Holiday of Lights at Bluefield City Park, City Manager Cecil Marson told the Bluefield Board of Directors Tuesday. “The biggest thing is we want to be able to sustain it and keep it going for the long term and so we’re looking at different options this year,” Marson told WVVA after the meeting. The donation-based, month-long event takes in $0.96 per visitor, Marson added. But, it costs $4.22 per visitor to operate, he continued. Among the proposed changes are reducing the number of days per week to Thursday to Sunday and charging visitors except for the week after Christmas. Marson said no changes have been made yet and will require board approval.

items.t: Domestic call lands Mercer County man in jail

According to the criminal complaint, West Virginia State Police responded to a domestic call in Bramwell on Oct.23. The Trooper was advised York’s elderly father already had a Domestic Violence Protective order against his son that still needed to be served and that York was allegedly fighting his father inside the residence. Cross, 43, of Beckley, pleaded guilty to possession with the intent to distribute cocaine and use and carry of a firearm during and in relation to a drug trafficking crime. Court documents and statements show that on Oct. 19, 2025, a law enforcement officer encountered Cross operating a four-wheeler on a Beckley street. A handgun fell out of his pants as he was taken to a law enforcement vehicle. Officers searched the four-wheeler and found approximately 51 grams of cocaine. Cross admitted that he intended to distribute the cocaine and used and carried the firearm in relation to his possession with intent to distribute cocaine.

items.t: How to use AI to budget for the holidays without overspending
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Holiday expenses often extend well beyond gifts and food, and those additional costs can add up quickly. Cherry Dale, vice president of financial education at Virginia Credit Union, said the first step to managing holiday spending is a simple list — before ever opening an AI tool like ChatGPT or Claude. Dale recommends listing everything planned for November and December spending, including travel, decorations, gifts and hosting costs. She said AI can help organize a budget, but personal information such as a name or banking details should never be entered. Dale said general, non-identifying details can still produce a useful, personalized budget. “You can put generic things like, ‘Hey, I’m hosting eight people for Thanksgiving, and I have six adults, two children. items.t: ‘You can’t go any higher’: American Airlines’ most senior flight attendant retires
items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. (Gray News) - American Airlines’ most senior flight attendant is retiring after nearly 64 years with the company. Carol Fair has worked as a flight attendant for 63 years. At 83, she is retiring at the top of American Airlines’ seniority list. “It’s time. I’ve enjoyed every minute of it. I made No. 1 out of 30,000. You can’t go any higher, so I might as well hang it up,” Fair said in an interview with Forbes . Her last trip was on an American Airlines flight from London to Charlotte, North Carolina, on Monday. A crowd celebrated Fair when the plane landed at Charlotte Douglas International Airport. Fair is a 2008 inductee of the North Carolina Transportation Hall of Fame and is also a member of the Tennessee Aviation Hall of Fame. Her career is also featured in an exhibit at the Sullenberger Aviation Museum.

items.t: Hilton Head man gets 20 years after shooting woman in head over argument
items.x: BEAUFORT COUNTY, S.C. (WTOC) - A Hilton Head Island man will spend 20 years in prison for shooting a woman in the head after a brief argument in an apartment parking lot. A Beaufort County jury found Bernard Garvin Jr., 35, guilty Wednesday of attempted murder and possession of a weapon during a violent crime in the June 9, 2023, shooting at Hilton Head Gardens on Southwood Park Drive. Prosecutors said Garvin shot the victim after she confronted him for fighting with another woman over a liquor bottle. He fired at least four shots from a 9mm handgun, grazing her in the head. She was treated in intensive care for possible bleeding on the brain. Circuit Court Judge Robert Bonds sentenced Garvin to 20 years, followed by five years’ probation. Garvin, known as “Berney,” was arrested Sept. 26, 2023, in Stockbridge, Ga., and extradited to Beaufort County. His record dates to 2011.

items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election

items.x: TOLEDO, Ohio ( WTVG /Gray News) - A cockroach attack forced the closure of a library in Ohio this week. Surveillance footage was released by the Toledo Lucas County Public Library, appearing to show a person throwing a box of cockroaches at a staff member on Tuesday at the Kent Branch Library. Surveillance footage apparently shows someone throwing a box of cockroaches at a library employee in Ohio. (Source: Toledo Lucas County Public Library) A library spokesperson confirmed the throwing of the box of cockroaches at the library worker on Collingwood Blvd. But it wasn’t immediately shared what led up to the cockroach attack. The library was said to have gone into restricted access before closing for the rest of the day for cleanup and remediation. The Kent Branch Library reopened Wednesday. Officials did not say whether anyone would be facing any charges.

items.t: 8-month-old dies after left alone in running bathtub, police say
items.x: STERLING, Va. (Gray News) - A Virginia woman was arrested after her 8-month-old died after being left unattended in a bathtub, according to authorities. Rosellena Pisani, 30, was arrested and charged with homicide, two counts of child abuse and three counts of child endangerment, a press release said. On Sept. 12, emergency medical personnel and sheriff’s deputies responded to the residence after receiving a call about an unresponsive infant. Investigators determined the baby had been left unsupervised in a bathtub with the water running. Three children, ranging in age from 8 months to 8 years old, were at home during the incident, according to police. Loudoun County Sheriff Mike Chapman called the baby’s death heartbreaking, saying caregivers have a fundamental duty to protect children. He added investigators remain committed to seeking justice in the case.

items.x: (Gray News) - Packaged salads produced by Taylor Farms have been recalled due to an undeclared allergen. According to the Food and Drug Administration, Taylor Farms is recalling its H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad because it may contain undeclared soy and tree nuts, specifically almonds. “People who have sensitivity or allergy to soy and tree nuts (almonds) may be at risk of a serious adverse reaction if they consume this product,” an FDA press release said. items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. Weil said the more skilled the service, the higher the price. “If you need someone to come in and help you prepare food, that’s less expensive than if you need someone to come in and provide nursing-level care,”

items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election

items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. items.t: The Exoneree Band: How a group of wrongfully convicted men found their voice through music
items.x: ( Aging Untold )— They don’t have the fame of The Beatles or the fortune of The Rolling Stones, but the members of The Exoneree band share something far more profound. Now, as free men, they are using the power of music to heal, to tell their stories, and to build a brotherhood unlike any other. The band was born out of the Innocence Network’s annual conference, a gathering that brings together wrongfully convicted people from across the country. In 2011, this group of musically inclined exonerees found each other, and what started as a jam session quickly turned into something more. “It turned into a really nice brotherhood of guys who were not only musicians but had went through the same thing of being wrongfully convicted,” one band member recalls. items.t: Breast cancer survivor faced hair loss during chemotherapy and reclaimed her identity
items.x: KANSAS CITY, Mo. ( Aging Untold ) — Hair loss is often the most common and visually striking side effect of chemotherapy, especially for women. Lisa Steinhauser, a breast cancer survivor, said she lost her hair and part of her identity during chemotherapy. Now she inspires patients to find strength during their own battle. Hair as part of her identity “So when I knew I was going to lose my hair, that was pretty hard because I had a lot of it,” she said. Hair has always been Steinhauser’s craft, artistry and expression. Diagnosis and treatment In December 2021, Steinhauser went in for a routine mammogram, and she said doctors found a spot they were concerned about. “I really was not expecting it to be anything at all, but it was,” she said. items.t: How to use AI to budget for the holidays without overspending
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Holiday expenses often extend well beyond gifts and food, and those additional costs can add up quickly. Cherry Dale, vice president of financial education at Virginia Credit Union, said the first step to managing holiday spending is a simple list — before ever opening an AI tool like ChatGPT or Claude. Dale recommends listing everything planned for November and December spending, including travel, decorations, gifts and hosting costs. She said AI can help organize a budget, but personal information such as a name or banking details should never be entered. Dale said general, non-identifying details can still produce a useful, personalized budget. “You can put generic things like, ‘Hey, I’m hosting eight people for Thanksgiving, and I have six adults, two children. They’re elite at stopping runs between the tackles, taking away receivers outside of the numbers and preventing deep passes down the field. Their pass rush is very real. items.t: ‘You can’t go any higher’: American Airlines’ most senior flight attendant retires
items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. (Gray News) - American Airlines’ most senior flight attendant is retiring after nearly 64 years with the company. Carol Fair has worked as a flight attendant for 63 years. At 83, she is retiring at the top of American Airlines’ seniority list. “It’s time. I’ve enjoyed every minute of it. I made No. 1 out of 30,000. You can’t go any higher, so I might as well hang it up,” Fair said in an interview with Forbes . Her last trip was on an American Airlines flight from London to Charlotte, North Carolina, on Monday. A crowd celebrated Fair when the plane landed at Charlotte Douglas International Airport. Fair is a 2008 inductee of the North Carolina Transportation Hall of Fame and is also a member of the Tennessee Aviation Hall of Fame. Her career is also featured in an exhibit at the Sullenberger Aviation Museum.

items.t: Deputies: Man with serious health issues missing
items.x: MEIGS COUNTY, Ohio (WSAZ) – Deputies need your help finding a missing man with serious health issues. Michael Hagaman, 76, was last seen around 5:40 p.m. Wednesday, the Meigs County Sheriff’s Office said. Deputies said Hagaman has Parkinson’s disease and “severe diabetes” and did not take his medications with him. “His health conditions make locating him a priority,” they said in a release. Hagaman is described as 6 feet tall and 211 pounds. He was last seen wearing a yellow T-shirt, blue jeans and black shoes. He was in a 2002 gold Ford F-150 truck. Anyone with information is asked to call the Meigs County Sheriff’s Office Dispatch at 740-992-6663 or their local 911 agency.

The closure started at 6:30 p.m. as crews worked to recover a semi-truck that crashed along Woodberry Way on Wednesday morning. Southbound traffic is being diverted to U.S 35, while northbound traffic will be turned around near the library and redirected toward Interstate 64. items.t: Road crews test winter weather equipment
items.x: CHARLESTON, W.Va. (WSAZ) - It’s always important to be prepared, and the city of Charleston is making sure its equipment is ready for all kinds of winter weather later this year. On Wednesday, the city’s Public Works Department hosted its annual salt parade. This event gives crews the opportunity to test out their snow removal equipment and salt spreaders well before all the snow and ice falls. Public Works Director Brent Webster said while the crews do their best to clean up the roads, it’s still important for people to drive carefully during the winter. “I think the city does a really great job of trying to monitor the forecast and treat the roads, but people should still ... drive as if the roads aren’t treated,” Webster said. Crews also shared information about the city’s fall leaf collection during the event.

items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election

Cherry Dale, vice president of financial education at Virginia Credit Union, said the first step to managing holiday spending is a simple list — before ever opening an AI tool like ChatGPT or Claude. items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election

items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election

items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. items.x: ATLANTA, Ga. (Atlanta News First) — A woman has been arrested after a 4-year-old child was found dead inside a southwest Atlanta townhome, according to police. Atlanta police located the child in a gated community in the 3500 block of Cardinal Drive SW on Monday. On Tuesday, the Wilkes County Sheriff’s Office said deputies arrested Jasmaine Smoak and charged her with murder. Atlanta police said Smoak, 32, was charged with second-degree cruelty to children and concealing the death of another. APD said Smoak was with three children, who have all been recovered, at the time of her arrest. One was injured and was taken to a hospital, they said. items.x: ATLANTA, Ga. (Atlanta News First) - ( InvestigateTV ) — Holiday expenses often extend well beyond gifts and food, and those additional costs can add up quickly. Cherry Dale, vice president of financial education at Virginia Credit Union, said the first step to managing holiday spending is a simple list — before ever opening an AI tool like ChatGPT or Claude. Dale recommends listing everything planned for November and December spending, including travel, decorations, gifts and hosting costs. She said AI can help organize a budget, but personal information such as a name or banking details should never be entered. items.x: ATLANTA, Ga. (Atlanta News First) — Three more measles cases have been reported in Macon County, the Georgia Department of Public Health (DPH) announced Tuesday. The three cases had previous contact with a measles case reported earlier this month. Like that previous case, all three were unvaccinated. The three new cases bring the statewide total to 25 this year. Ten cases of measles were reported statewide in 2025, DPH said. Measles, a highly contagious disease, spreads through the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes. The virus can remain in the air for up to two hours after an infected person leaves, according to DPH. The department said symptoms typically appear 7–14 days after exposure but can take up to 21 days. items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election

items.x: TOLEDO, Ohio ( WTVG /Gray News) - A cockroach attack forced the closure of a library in Ohio this week. Surveillance footage was released by the Toledo Lucas County Public Library, appearing to show a person throwing a box of cockroaches at a staff member on Tuesday at the Kent Branch Library. Surveillance footage apparently shows someone throwing a box of cockroaches at a library employee in Ohio. (Source: Toledo Lucas County Public Library) A library spokesperson confirmed the throwing of the box of cockroaches at the library worker on Collingwood Blvd. But it wasn’t immediately shared what led up to the cockroach attack. The library was said to have gone into restricted access before closing for the rest of the day for cleanup and remediation. The Kent Branch Library reopened Wednesday. Officials did not say whether anyone would be facing any charges.

items.t: Some packaged salads recalled for undeclared allergens
items.x: (Gray News) - Packaged salads produced by Taylor Farms have been recalled due to an undeclared allergen. According to the Food and Drug Administration, Taylor Farms is recalling its H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad because it may contain undeclared soy and tree nuts, specifically almonds. “People who have sensitivity or allergy to soy and tree nuts (almonds) may be at risk of a serious adverse reaction if they consume this product,” an FDA press release said. So far there have not been any illnesses or “adverse reactions” reported in connection with the recall. The salads were sold in H-E-B stores across Texas. They can be identified by their UPC code, 041220300457, and their best-by date, Oct. 30, 2026. Customers are asked not to eat the recalled salads and to throw them away or return them to the store for a refund.

items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. Weil said the more skilled the service, the higher the price. “If you need someone to come in and help you prepare food, that’s less expensive than if you need someone to come in and provide nursing-level care,”

items.t: 500K gallons of sewage spilled into York County creek, officials say
items.x: LAKE WYLIE, S.C. (WBTV) - An estimated 500,000 gallons of sewage were spilled into a creek in York County on Monday. County officials confirmed that the Little Allison Creek pump station lost power on Oct. 26. The sewage then spilled into the creek. The county said as soon as the spill was discovered, it contacted the South Carolina Department of Environmental Services. County staff were reportedly working with state environmental officials to resolve the issue. York County said in an Oct. 27 news release that it has “prioritized a fix to the pump station.” In that same release, the county said it “deeply regret[s]” the spill and apologized. Officials did not address in the news release any water safety impacts regarding the sewage spill. Little Allison Creek feeds into the South Carolina side of Lake Wylie. items.t: How to use AI to budget for the holidays without overspending
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Holiday expenses often extend well beyond gifts and food, and those additional costs can add up quickly. Cherry Dale, vice president of financial education at Virginia Credit Union, said the first step to managing holiday spending is a simple list — before ever opening an AI tool like ChatGPT or Claude. Dale recommends listing everything planned for November and December spending, including travel, decorations, gifts and hosting costs. items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election

items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. Weil said the more skilled the service, the higher the price. “If you need someone to come in and help you prepare food, that’s less expensive than if you need someone to come in and provide nursing-level care,”

items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election

items.t: Library says person threw box of cockroaches at a staff member, prompting closure
items.x: TOLEDO, Ohio ( WTVG /Gray News) - A cockroach attack forced the closure of a library in Ohio this week. Surveillance footage was released by the Toledo Lucas County Public Library, appearing to show a person throwing a box of cockroaches at a staff member on Tuesday at the Kent Branch Library. Surveillance footage apparently shows someone throwing a box of cockroaches at a library employee in Ohio. (Source: Toledo Lucas County Public Library) A library spokesperson confirmed the throwing of the box of cockroaches at the library worker on Collingwood Blvd. But it wasn’t immediately shared what led up to the cockroach attack. The library was said to have gone into restricted access before closing for the rest of the day for cleanup and remediation. The Kent Branch Library reopened Wednesday. Officials did not say whether anyone would be facing any charges.

items.t: 8-month-old dies after left alone in running bathtub, police say
items.x: STERLING, Va. (Gray News) - A Virginia woman was arrested after her 8-month-old died after being left unattended in a bathtub, according to authorities. Rosellena Pisani, 30, was arrested and charged with homicide, two counts of child abuse and three counts of child endangerment, a press release said. On Sept. 12, emergency medical personnel and sheriff’s deputies responded to the residence after receiving a call about an unresponsive infant. Investigators determined the baby had been left unsupervised in a bathtub with the water running. Three children, ranging in age from 8 months to 8 years old, were at home during the incident, according to police. Loudoun County Sheriff Mike Chapman called the baby’s death heartbreaking, saying caregivers have a fundamental duty to protect children. items.t: Some packaged salads recalled for undeclared allergens
items.x: (Gray News) - Packaged salads produced by Taylor Farms have been recalled due to an undeclared allergen. According to the Food and Drug Administration, Taylor Farms is recalling its H-E-B Backyard BBQ Chop Salad because it may contain undeclared soy and tree nuts, specifically almonds. “People who have sensitivity or allergy to soy and tree nuts (almonds) may be at risk of a serious adverse reaction if they consume this product,” an FDA press release said. So far there have not been any illnesses or “adverse reactions” reported in connection with the recall. The salads were sold in H-E-B stores across Texas. They can be identified by their UPC code, 041220300457, and their best-by date, Oct. 30, 2026. Customers are asked not to eat the recalled salads and to throw them away or return them to the store for a refund.

items.t: Long-term care costs rose about 50% in five years, report finds
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — The cost of long-term care jumped nearly 50% in five years, while income for older households rose just 22%, according to a new AARP report . The report found long-term services and supports are becoming even less affordable for middle-class Americans. Alan Weil, senior vice president for public policy at AARP, said the gap is the most important finding. “Between 2019 and 2024, a five-year period, the cost of most long-term care services went up about 50%, but the incomes for older households only went up by about 22%,” Weil said. “So the gap between what people can afford and what it costs has grown.” The AARP also looked at what different types of care cost. Weil said the more skilled the service, the higher the price. “If you need someone to come in and help you prepare food, that’s less expensive than if you need someone to come in and provide nursing-level care,”

items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election

items.t: JMU expert urges cybersecurity and awareness amid AI-assisted scams
items.x: HARRISONBURG, Va. (WHSV) - Experts say it’s getting harder to tell what’s real and what’s a scam, as scammers now turn to artificial intelligence to make them sound even more convincing. items.t: Virginia SNAP soda restrictions begin Sunday, but some sugary drinks remain eligible
items.x: RICHMOND, Va. (WWBT) - Starting Sunday, Nov. 1, Virginians will no longer be able to use Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits to purchase soda and certain energy drinks. The restrictions include regular, diet and zero-sugar soda, carbonated energy drinks and other carbonated beverages containing five grams or more of added sugar per serving. But some drinks containing added sugar, including lemonade, iced tea and non-carbonated sports drinks, will remain eligible. That distinction is raising questions among nutrition experts about the reasoning behind the new rules. Why are some sugary drinks still eligible? items.t: Democrats hold fundraising advantage over Republicans in 5th and 6th district races
items.x: ROANOKE, Va. (WDBJ) - Democratic challengers have a fundraising advantage in Virginia’s 5th and 6th Congressional districts, according to Federal Election Commission filing reports released a week before Election Day. Republicans have held both districts for years. Unlike the last few Congressional races in the area, Democrats are raising more money as they try to flip the two districts that are typically Republican strongholds. Candidates across the country have raised almost $3.7 billion for this year’s election, according to Federal Election Commission data. Democrats have raised about $2.2 billion. Republicans have raised around $1.5 billion. All 10 of the top 10 national fundraisers are Democrat candidates. The House is raising almost $1 billion more than the Senate. There are 400 more House seats open than Senate seats, so proportionally more money is being raised for Senate races.

items.t: How to use AI to budget for the holidays without overspending
items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Holiday expenses often extend well beyond gifts and food, and those additional costs can add up quickly. Cherry Dale, vice president of financial education at Virginia Credit Union, said the first step to managing holiday spending is a simple list — before ever opening an AI tool like ChatGPT or Claude. Dale recommends listing everything planned for November and December spending, including travel, decorations, gifts and hosting costs. She said AI can help organize a budget, but personal information such as a name or banking details should never be entered. Dale said general, non-identifying details can still produce a useful, personalized budget. “You can put generic things like, ‘Hey, I’m hosting eight people for Thanksgiving, and I have six adults, two children. items.x: ( InvestigateTV ) — Holiday expenses often extend well beyond gifts and food, and those additional costs can add up quickly. Cherry Dale, vice president of financial education at Virginia Credit Union, said the first step to managing holiday spending is a simple list — before ever opening an AI tool like ChatGPT or Claude. items.t: Meet the 83-year-old marina keeper preserving hundreds of years of Vermont history
items.x: ORWELL, Vt. ( Aging Untold ) — At one of the narrowest points on Lake Champlain, a piece of Vermont’s maritime past is still standing — and still in use. For more than 30 years, 83-year-old Pat Ullom and her son have run Chipman Point Marina. Chipman Point was once where “all the goods landed,” Ullom said. A landing point for 1800s commerce In the 1800s, the area was a busy maritime community close to New York state. The marina’s main stone building was built in 1810 and quarried from the property itself. Boats once unloaded cargo directly into the building through its doorways, and the second floor functioned “more like a grocery store.” Ullom said the beams inside are original to the building. “Yeah, yeah, I do that a lot,” Ullom said, when asked if she ever looks out at the water and imagines what the property looked like in 1810. items.t: How going outside in nature could ease stress
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — There is something about nature that makes us feel instantly connected. items.t: For politics, what is an October surprise?
items.x: WASHINGTON (Gray DC) - An October surprise is an event that could shake up an election, but does it often make the difference? Matt Dallek, a professor of political management at George Washington University, described it as “an event that, at least in theory, has the potential to shake up an election, something that people did not foresee coming that upends the debate.” He said the term dates back to around the 1980 election, when President Jimmy Carter failed to secure the release of American hostages being held in Iran before November 4, 1980, election day. Carter lost to Republican rival Ronald Reagan. Several surprises have occurred in the years since. Surprises can be driven by a campaign or by news events. Examples include Iran-Contra-related indictments in 1992 and the global financial collapse in 2008. Dallek said those surprises likely did not change the outcome of the election
