items.t: Special needs teacher accused of pouring hot sauce on student’s tongue as a punishment
items.x: HOUSTON COUNTY, Ala. ( WTVY /Gray News) - An Alabama special needs teacher is facing child abuse charges after deputies say she poured hot sauce on a student’s tongue. Heather Varner Hunter, a 46-year-old special needs teacher at Cottonwood Elementary School, allegedly used hot sauce to punish a student for sticking out their tongue in September. A Houston County Sheriff’s Office investigation followed. Jail records show Hunter was arrested Monday afternoon. She is no longer employed by the Houston County School System, according to Superintendent Brandy White. White said the school system cooperated fully with authorities, and all information has been turned over to the Alabama Department of Human Resources. items.t: Former true-crime producer accused of posing as aircraft heiress added to FBI most-wanted list
items.x: (Gray News) - A 75-year-old woman who allegedly posed as an heiress to steal more than $14 million has been added to the FBI’s Most Wanted list. According to the FBI, Mary Carole McDonnell is accused of posing as the heiress to the McDonnell Aircraft family with an $80 million secret trust. The McDonnell Aircraft Corporation was an aerospace manufacturer best known for its military aircrafts. The FBI said the alleged scheme began in July 2017 and lasted until May 2018. McDonnell allegedly obtained $14.7 million from Banc of California, as well as an additional $15 million from other financial institutions. On Dec. 12, 2018, a federal arrest warrant was issued for McDonnell. She faces charges of bank fraud and aggravated identity theft. McDonnell is described as 5-foot-7 with blond hair and blue eyes. items.t: Teenager charged in hit-and-run that killed 6-year-old getting off the bus
items.x: CHARLOTTE, N.C. ( WBTV /Gray News) - A 17-year-old was charged in connection with a hit-and-run that killed a 6-year-old girl in Charlotte last week, according to authorities. Charlotte police announced Monday that Lachevis Finnie, 17, was arrested in the hit-and-run death of 6-year-old Mariana Espinoza. He was charged with felony hit-and-run resulting in death. Espinoza was hit by a car while crossing at the intersection last Friday in east Charlotte. Espinoza, a student at Devonshire Elementary School, had just gotten off the school bus. Police said Espinoza was taken to a hospital with life-threatening injuries and died there the following day. Doorbell camera footage obtained by WBTV on Monday shows the moments before Espinoza was hit. items.t: Aging Untold: Hospice doesn’t have to happen at home
items.x: ( Aging Untold ) — On this episode of Aging Untold, we explore compassionate hospice care options beyond the home, focusing on comfort, dignity and family support. Plus, we share practical advice for older adults stepping up to raise school-aged kids and navigating today’s modern classrooms. Then, a breast cancer survivor opens up about the emotional toll of chemotherapy-induced hair loss and how she reclaimed her identity and strength. items.t: The Exoneree Band: How a group of wrongfully convicted men found their voice through music
items.x: ( Aging Untold )— They don’t have the fame of The Beatles or the fortune of The Rolling Stones, but the members of The Exoneree band share something far more profound. Now, as free men, they are using the power of music to heal, to tell their stories, and to build a brotherhood unlike any other. The band was born out of the Innocence Network’s annual conference, a gathering that brings together wrongfully convicted people from across the country. In 2011, this group of musically inclined exonerees found each other, and what started as a jam session quickly turned into something more. “It turned into a really nice brotherhood of guys who were not only musicians but had went through the same thing of being wrongfully convicted,” one band member recalls. items.t: ‘McMillan & Wife’ actress Susan Saint James dies at 80
items.x: (Gray News) - Emmy-winning actress Susan Saint James has died. She was 80 years old. Saint James, who starred in “McMillan & Wife,” “Kate & Allie” and “The Name Game,” died Monday after being diagnosed with pancreatic cancer, according to People . Her family said she was “generous with her time and energy, which she valued more than money, and instinctively drawn to whoever needed lifting up,” in a statement to People. Saint James “never met a stranger” and “taught her children to pause, be kind and look out for other people,” her family said. “Every person she met became the most important person in the room at that moment, from a fellow board member to the clerk at the shoe store, who usually walked away knowing her entire life story,” her family said.
